Invoices are raised per client, optionally against a project, with HSN codes and a GST rate per line; the CGST and SGST totals are computed from the lines every time rather than stored, and each invoice moves from draft to sent to paid.

Nothing is ever hard-deleted: a removed record stops showing but stays in the database, and deleting at all needs an owner, admin or manager.

## What should a design studio ask before choosing software?

1. **Does it hold the design side and the workshop side together** — projects, site visits, workshop orders and vendors — or only one of them?
2. **Can it pay daily-wage workers** from real attendance, with advances deducted, not from a separate notebook?
3. **Does it check vendor and freight bills** against what they should cost, or just record them?
4. **If you run two companies, does each invoice carry the right company's name and GSTIN** from one system?
5. **Who can see the money?** Staff logging petty cash shouldn't see the bank account — enforced by the server, not by hiding a menu.

## What did the owners say?

> "They really took the time to understand our concerns and requirements, and the system was built the way we had envisioned it. It has brought much more structure, visibility, and control to the way we operate."
>
> — Sachi & Haripriya, owners of Savistar and Saag

## Boundary

This is one shared app for two related businesses, not a multi-tenant platform: adding an unrelated third company would mean a different design, not a new setting.

Quotations were added in October 2026 and haven't been used on a real project yet: the studio's own BOQ library (started from our [interior BOQ item library](/boq/items)), quantities from site dimensions, and payment stages that become draft invoices once a quote is accepted. Quotes and invoices charge CGST and SGST, or IGST when the site is in another state. There is no 3D design or mood boards, and no client portal — clients are served by the team, not by a login. The free [interior BOQ checker](/boq/check) on this site runs the same line checks without an account.

title: What changed with the Boilers Act 2025 and IBR 2026

body:
## When did IBR 2026 replace IBR 1950?

The Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026 replaced the Indian Boiler Regulations, 1950 on 1 October 2026, the day they were published in the Gazette of India (Extraordinary, No. 596). The Central Boilers Board made them under section 40 of the Boilers Act, 2025, which itself repealed the Boilers Act, 1923.

The supersession is "except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession", so what was done under IBR 1950 before 1 October 2026 is not undone by the change.

## Were the IBR forms renumbered?

Yes. The IBR 2026 forms run from Form I to Form XXIII, and most folder documents changed number. The maker's certificate of manufacture and test, Form III under IBR 1950, is now Form IV Part A. The Inspecting Authority's certificate, Form II(1) or II(2), is now Form I Part B or Part C. The steel maker's certificate, Form IV, is now Form V Part A.

Every form, with its old name, is on [the IBR 2026 forms list](/ibr/forms).

## Can IBR certificates be filed electronically now?

Yes. Under regulation 8 of IBR 2026, the certificates, drawings and specifications that go with a boiler's registration application may be submitted electronically with digital signatures. Well-known pipe and tube makers may also issue their certificates (Form IV Part B and Part C) online with a digital signature.

## How long must boiler records be kept under IBR 2026?

Regulation 308 sets three periods. The Inspecting Authority keeps a boiler's certificates and approved drawings for at least three years after registration. The owner keeps them for the entire life of the boiler, and hands them to any new owner. The manufacturer keeps them, including Form V Part B, for at least five years. See [boiler record keeping under IBR 2026](/ibr/record-keeping).

## What changed for boiler manufacturers?

A firm seeking recognition as a manufacturer applies to an Inspecting Authority in its own state with the manufacturer questionnaire, Form III, which is new in IBR 2026 (regulation 7(1)(b)(v)). Recognition lasts three years, and renewal is applied for at least ninety days before it expires (regulation 7(4)). Components can be erected at site on the strength of a final inspection report in Form VIII approved by the Competent Person (regulation 293(2)). The steel maker's certificate, now Form V Part A, gives ultimate tensile strength in kilograms per square millimetre; the IBR 1950 Form IV gave it in tons.

## What changed in registration?

Under regulation 300 of IBR 2026, the Inspector inspects the boiler, conducts the hydraulic test and issues a provisional order in Form X, under section 14 of the Boilers Act, 2025; under IBR 1950 the provisional order was Form V. The boiler's record is the Memorandum of Inspection Book, now Form XI. See [documents for boiler registration](/ibr/registration-documents).

title: How long boiler records must be kept under IBR 2026

body:
## How long must a boiler manufacturer keep IBR records?

A boiler manufacturer keeps the boiler's records for at least five years under regulation 308(4) of IBR 2026. The same rule covers makers of economisers and steam pipes. The records are the Inspecting Authority's certificates (Form I Part B or C), the component certificates (Form IV Parts B, C and D), the material certificates (Form V Parts A and B), the economiser certificates (Forms XV and XVI) and copies of the approved drawings.

## How long must the boiler owner keep them?

The owner keeps the boiler's certificates and approved drawings for the entire life of the boiler under regulation 308(2). If the boiler is sold, the records go to the new owner, who keeps them on the same terms (regulation 308(3)).

## How long does the Inspecting Authority keep them?

The Inspecting Authority keeps a boiler's records, including Form IV Part A, for at least three years after registration, and may then send them to the owner (regulation 308(1)).

## Where is the boiler's inspection book kept?

The Memorandum of Inspection Book, [Form XI](/ibr/forms/form-xi), is kept in the Chief Inspector's office except when the Competent Person needs it for an inspection (regulation 306). The Chief Inspector also keeps a registration book with the same particulars (regulation 307). If a boiler moves to another state, both books go to that state's Chief Inspector on request (regulation 309).

## When can the original certificates be asked for?

Within three years of a boiler's registration, if a question arises about its fitness for the approved working pressure, the Chief Inspector can ask the owner to obtain and furnish the original documents (regulation 8(d)(ii)).

## Why does five years matter for a manufacturer?

Five years of certificates for every boiler made is a large archive. In one boiler manufacturer's sample, each [material test certificate](/systems/material-test-certificate) was used across about 3.2 boilers, so one certificate is evidence in several folders. The system Ahrom Labs built for that manufacturer keeps them in one bank indexed by certificate, cast and plate number, rather than copied into each folder. See [how that system keeps test certificates](/notes/ibr-statutory-folder-from-bom).

title: Boiler registration under IBR 2026: documents checklist
answer: Under regulation 8 of IBR 2026, a boiler's registration application goes to the Chief Inspector with four sets of documents: the Inspecting Authority's certificate (Form I Part B or C), the maker's certificate (Form IV Part A), drawings, and the material certificates (Form V Part A, with the Form V Part B extract).

Regulations 8, 300, 301 and 310.

checks.quote: The engraving shall be complete and ready for verification within one month from the date of receipt of registry number, and the fact shall be reported to the Chief Inspector of Boiler within this period.
A certificate in Form-I(Part-B) or Form-I(Part-C), as the case may be, from an Inspecting Authority, certifying that the material was tested and the boiler was built under their supervision
A certificate in Form-IV(Part-A) of manufacture and test signed by the maker of the boiler or its representative

In case of shop assembled boilers, drawings to an appropriate scale showing the principal dimensions, sections, maker’s number, position of Inspecting Authority’s stamp, bill of material, welding details and design parameters.
A certificate in Form-V(Part-A) from the steel maker and a certificate from the maker of the plates or bars
The extract of all test certificates of materials used in boiler and boiler components in Form-V(Part-B) along with Form-IV(Part-A).
In the case of fusion welded drums, diagram of weld repairs and temperature charts of heat-treatment shall also be furnished.
Alloy steel materials used in creep range in furnace or super-heater zone
two numbers of 1000 hour stress rupture tests shall be carried out at 50°C above the maximum service temperature for each grade of alloy steel and Nickel alloys
all boilers of capacity less than 20 tons per hour shall carry all the mountings or fittings certificates in respective forms
the Inspector shall conduct hydraulic test as per requirements of regulations 298 and a provisional order under section 14 in Form-X shall be issued after the hydraulic test.
after issue of registry number, the Inspector shall conduct steam test as per regulation 299 and enter the details of steam test in Form-XI.
The registry number of every boiler shall, within a period of one month from the date of receipt thereof, shall be cut in the front plate

body:
## Which documents go with a boiler registration application?

Regulation 8 of the Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026 lists what goes to the Chief Inspector with an application to register a boiler. They may be filed on paper or electronically with digital signatures.

1. **The Inspecting Authority's certificate:** [Form I Part B](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-b) for a shop-assembled boiler, or [Form I Part C](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-c) for one assembled at site. [Form I Part D](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-d) replaces either when permitted variations apply.
2. **The maker's certificate of manufacture and test:** [Form IV Part A](/ibr/forms/form-iv-part-a), signed by the maker.
3. **Drawings:** for a shop-assembled boiler, drawings showing principal dimensions, sections, maker's number, stamp position, bill of material, welding details and design parameters.
4. **Material certificates:** the steel maker's [Form V Part A](/ibr/forms/form-v-part-a), and the [Form V Part B](/ibr/forms/form-v-part-b) extract of every [material test certificate](/systems/material-test-certificate) used.

## What else is needed for some boilers?

Fusion-welded drums need a diagram of weld repairs and the heat-treatment temperature charts (regulation 8(d)(v)). Alloy steels used in the creep range in the furnace or superheater zone need two 1,000-hour stress rupture tests for each grade (regulation 8(d)(vi)). Boilers under 20 tons per hour carry all their mountings and fittings certificates; at 20 tons per hour and above, mountings for site-assembled boilers may be supplied separately (regulation 8(d)(vii)).

## What happens after the application is filed?

Under regulation 300, the Inspector inspects the boiler at site for transit damage and checks the maker's certificate against the boiler. The Inspector then conducts the hydraulic test and issues a provisional order in [Form X](/ibr/forms/form-x), so the boiler can be used while registration completes. The particulars and test results go into the Memorandum of Inspection Book, [Form XI](/ibr/forms/form-xi), which goes to the Chief Inspector with the maker's papers. Once the registry number is issued, the Inspector conducts a steam test and enters it in Form XI (regulation 300(4)); the certificate for use, [Form XII](/ibr/forms/form-xii), follows (regulation 310).

## When is the registry number engraved?

Within one month of receiving it, the registry number is cut into the boiler's front plate or wherever the Inspector points out, and the engraving is reported to the Chief Inspector within the same month (regulation 301). The number sits below the state's letters, for example GT for Gujarat and MR for Maharashtra; a small industrial boiler's number carries an "S" prefix.

A boiler designed to the ASME Code still goes through IBR registration in India. Where IBR 2026 accepts ASME designs, materials and inspection, and how the ASME paperwork lines up with these forms, is in [ASME vs IBR 2026](/asme/asme-vs-ibr) and [ASME data reports](/asme/data-reports).

title: Small industrial boilers under IBR 2026
answer: Under IBR 2026 a small industrial boiler is a shell boiler up to 7 kg/cm² (g) holding more than 25 and up to 500 litres, or a coil, once-through or water tube boiler up to 12 kg/cm² (g) and 150 litres. Its certificate of manufacture and test is Form XXII, which was Form XVII under IBR 1950.

body:
## What counts as a small industrial boiler under IBR 2026?

A small industrial boiler, under regulation 546 of IBR 2026, is one of two kinds. A shell type boiler working up to 7 kg/cm² (g), with a volumetric capacity of more than 25 litres and up to 500 litres, measured from the feed check valve to the main steam stop valve. Or a coil type, once-through or water tube boiler working up to 12 kg/cm² (g), with a capacity of up to 150 litres. A boiler combining both kinds is held to 7 kg/cm² (g) and 500 litres in total.

## Which stages are inspected for a small shell boiler?

An Inspecting Authority inspects a small industrial boiler during construction (regulation 550). For a shell type boiler, regulation 551 sets four stages: material identification and inspection; each component after welding and drilling; assembly of the boiler; and the hydraulic test. A welded boiler is tested at twice its design pressure, and the maker provides a test coupon for root and face bend tests.

## Which certificate does a small industrial boiler need?

A small industrial boiler's certificate of manufacture and test is [Form XXII](/ibr/forms/form-xxii) (regulation 555(2)). Under IBR 1950 this was Form XVII, which also covered small solar boilers; they now have their own Form XXIII. If the boiler's plate is too small to stamp every detail, the certificate carries them, but the name, works number and year of make are always stamped or shown on the boiler (regulation 553(2)).

## Which plates can a small industrial boiler use, and is a steel maker's certificate needed?

A small industrial boiler's plates are IS 2062 fully killed steel or equivalent, at least 6 mm thick for the shell and heads, and at least 8 mm where heads serve as tube sheets for rolled-in tubes (regulation 548(2)(a)). The steel maker's certificate in Form V Part A is not required for IS 2062 plates, provided every other certification requirement is met (regulation 548(2)(b)).

## How is a small industrial boiler's registry number marked?

A small industrial boiler's registry number carries an "S" prefix below the state's letters, for example "GT" over "S-" and the number for a boiler registered in Gujarat (regulation 301(1)(c)).

title: How to make an interior BOQ, step by step
answer: Make an interior BOQ in 7 steps: read the drawings and finish schedule, split the work room by room and trade, pick each item and its unit, measure and state how, name the material, size, finish and hardware, list exclusions, then price it. A line two contractors would read differently is the line that causes the dispute.
description: Making an interior BOQ from drawings in 7 steps, with the units, specifications and exclusions each line needs, and a sample.

image.alt: A floor plan with an architect's scale ruler resting on it and one room traced over in pencil.

sources.title: IS 1200, Method of measurement of building and civil engineering works (all parts)

body:
## 1. Start from the drawings and the finish schedule

A [BOQ](/systems/bill-of-quantities) is only as complete as the drawings behind it: plans, ceiling plans, elevations of every joinery unit, the electrical layout and a finish schedule naming each material. Anything not drawn is either missing from the BOQ or priced as a guess.

## 2. Split the work by room, then by trade

Group lines room by room (kitchen, master bedroom, bathroom 1) and within each room by trade: civil, false ceiling, flooring, carpentry, painting, electrical, plumbing. The client reads it by room; contractors price it by trade; a site supervisor checks it against both.

## 3. Pick each item and its unit

Use the unit the trade prices in: sq ft for ceilings, floors, panelling and wardrobes; running ft for kitchen cabinets, skirting and coves; number for doors, fittings and drawers; point for wiring. A wardrobe in running ft and another in sq ft can't be compared. The [item library](/boq/items) gives the usual unit for 41 items.

## 4. Measure, and say how

For civil-type work, IS 1200 sets the method ([measurement rules](/boq/measurement-rules) has each part's rules): Part 10 for ceilings and linings, Part 11 for floor finishes, dado and skirting, Part 13 for painting building surfaces, Part 21 for woodwork, which is measured net as fixed with nothing added for shape or joints. Modular work has no such standard, so the line must say it: "measured by front elevation, loft excluded".

## 5. Name what it's made of

Every joinery line names the board and its grade (for example IS 303 BWP plywood), the thickness, the finish inside and out, the edge band and the hardware make. Leave one out and the cheapest version of it is what gets priced. See [material specifications](/boq/material-specifications).

## 6. List what's excluded and what the client supplies

Countertops, appliances, light fittings, sanitaryware and loose furniture are often bought by the client or priced separately. Write them down as excluded or as their own lines; an unlisted exclusion becomes an argument at the final bill.

## 7. Price it, then issue it

Rates come last: from your own rate analysis or from contractors pricing the same lines. GST is added at the quotation, not in the rates. Changes after this point are [variations](/boq/variation-orders), priced as new lines rather than by editing old ones.

## A sample

| No | Description | Unit | Qty |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kitchen base cabinets in 18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood carcass, acrylic shutters, 2 mm PVC edge band, soft-close hinges and channels of [make]; measured by running length, excluding countertop | running ft | 14 |
| 2 | Kitchen wall cabinets 700 mm high in 18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood, laminate shutters, 2 mm PVC edge band, [make] hinges; measured by running length | running ft | 12 |
| 3 | 20 mm granite countertop 625 mm deep, edge moulded, including sink and hob cut-outs | running ft | 14 |
| 4 | Hinged wardrobe in 18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood, 1 mm laminate outside, 0.8 mm inside, 2 mm PVC edge band, [make] soft-close hinges; measured by front elevation, excluding loft | sq ft | 64 |
| 5 | Gypsum board false ceiling 12.5 mm on GI framing, joints taped; measured by plan area of the flat field, excluding coves | sq ft | 180 |

Paste your own into the [checker](/boq/check) to see what each line leaves open, or start from the [Excel template](/boq/template).

## Boundary

The steps and units are common practice for interior work in India; IS 1200 governs only the trades it covers. Quantities, rates and the GST treatment of your contract are yours, and your CA's, to settle.

title: Board standards for an interior BOQ: IS 303, IS 710 and others
answer: An interior BOQ names the board by its Indian Standard and grade, because "plywood" alone can be priced as the cheapest sheet in the market. IS 303 covers general-purpose plywood (MR, and BWR, renamed BWP by amendment), IS 710 marine plywood, IS 1659 block boards, and IS 3087 and IS 12823 particle boards.
description: The Indian Standards for plywood, block board and particle board, and how to write a joinery BOQ line that can't be substituted.

image.alt: A stack of five board offcuts cut to show their edges: layered plywood, block board with a core of timber strips, particle board, a plain board, and particle board with a thin dark top sheet.

sources.title: IS 303:2024, Plywood for general purposes
IS 303:1989, Plywood for general purposes (third revision), public copy
sources.publisher: Bureau of Indian Standards, via Public.Resource.Org

body:
## Why the standard goes in the line

"18 mm plywood with laminate" describes sheets that differ several times over in price and in how they survive a wet kitchen. Naming the standard and grade fixes what is being priced and gives the site something to check: the grade is marked on each sheet.

## Plywood: IS 303 and IS 710

- **IS 303, plywood for general purposes.** The 1989 edition grades plywood by the bond of its adhesive: MR (moisture resistant) and BWR (boiling water resistant), and an amendment renamed BWR as BWP. It also names faces by quality: AA, AB and BB. IS 303:2024 is the current edition in the BIS catalogue; check its grade names when you specify.
- **IS 710, marine plywood**, for wet areas such as vanities and sink bases, where a BOQ wants more than BWP.

## Block board and particle boards

- **IS 1659, block boards**: a core of timber strips between veneers, used for long shelves and doors.
- **IS 3087**: medium-density particle boards for general purposes.
- **IS 12823**: prelaminated particle boards, the factory-laminated board of most low-cost modular units.
- **IS 2202 (Part 1)**: wooden flush door shutters, solid core, with plywood face panels.

Boards sold under trade names (HDHMR, for example) should be named by product and maker in the line, with the maker's test certificate asked for.

## Writing a line that can't be substituted

A joinery line names five things:

1. The board, its standard and grade: "18 mm IS 303 BWP plywood carcass".
2. The thickness of each part, if carcass, shutters and back differ.
3. The finish inside and out: "1 mm laminate outside, 0.8 mm inside", or acrylic, veneer, PU.
4. The edge band: "2 mm PVC edge band".
5. The hardware make, or "[make] or equal" with the reference named.

How joinery is measured, net as fixed and by area with its thickness, is in [measurement rules](/boq/measurement-rules). The [checker](/boq/check) flags a joinery line missing any of these; the [item library](/boq/items) has a line to start from for each item.

## Boundary

Standards are cited by number and title from the BIS catalogue, not quoted; the standard governs. Which grade a job needs is a design decision this page does not make.

title: How interior work is measured for a BOQ (IS 1200)
answer: Floors, ceilings, paint and woodwork have an Indian Standard for measurement, IS 1200: measure net as fixed, deduct openings only above a set size, and price skirting by running length with its height stated. Modular kitchens and wardrobes have none, so a BOQ line must say its basis: the same wardrobe can be 60 sq ft or 8 running ft.

body:
## Which trades have a measurement standard

IS 1200 is the Indian Standard method of measuring building work, in parts by trade. Four parts cover most of an interior job; modular furniture is not one of them.

| Work | Standard | Unit in the standard |
|---|---|---|
| False ceilings and wall linings | IS 1200 (Part 10) | square metres, measured flat |
| Floors, dado and skirting | IS 1200 (Part 11) | square metres; skirting in running metres |
| Paint on walls and ceilings | IS 1200 (Part 13) | square metres |
| Woodwork, panelling and joinery | IS 1200 (Part 21) | square metres for boarding, with its thickness |
| Modular kitchens, wardrobes, lofts | None | whatever the BOQ states |

Interior quotes in India are usually written in sq ft and running ft rather than the standard's metric units: 1 sq m is 10.764 sq ft, and 1 m is 3.281 ft. The rules below are the same in either unit.

## Floors, dado and skirting

Part 11 measures floor finishes and dado in square metres, and skirting in running metres with its height stated; mitres, stops and returned ends are part of the skirting item, not extra. Nothing is deducted for embedded items up to 0.1 m² each. A strip of finish 30 cm wide or less that doesn't match the general floor is measured by running length; wider than that, by area.

For a BOQ that means three lines, not one: the floor by area, the skirting by length with its height, and any border or threshold strip as its own line.

## False ceilings

Part 10 measures ceilings flat, in square metres, net as fixed. An opening up to 0.4 m² (a light cut-out, a grille) is not deducted and not charged for; a bigger opening is deducted in full and the work of forming it is measured separately. Boarding on curved surfaces up to 15 cm wide is its own item.

Coves, drops and bands are not flat ceiling, which is why the [false ceiling items](/boq/items/false-ceiling) price them by running length: say their girth (height plus width) in the line.

## Paint

Part 13 measures walls, ceilings and sloping surfaces separately, and every item states the number of coats. Openings up to 0.5 m² each are not deducted, and their reveals are not added. A line reading "painting, 900 sq ft" leaves out both: which surfaces, and how many coats of what.

## Woodwork and panelling

Part 21 measures woodwork net as fixed: nothing is added for shape, joints or wastage. Boarding, which the standard says covers panelling, shelves and almirah linings, is measured in square metres with its finished thickness stated. Wastage belongs in the rate, not the quantity.

## Modular kitchens, wardrobes and lofts

No Indian Standard sets how modular units are measured, so the trade uses several bases, and two quotes on different bases can't be compared:

- **Kitchen cabinets**: usually by running length along the wall, base and wall units as separate lines, corners counted once. Say whether the plinth and back panels are included.
- **Wardrobes**: usually by front elevation, height × width. Say whether the loft, side panels and internal drawers are in it; lofts are often a separate line.
- **Tall units and accessories**: per unit, size stated.

The same wardrobe, 8 ft wide and 7 ft 6 in high, is 60 sq ft by elevation or 8 running ft along the wall. At ₹1,450 per sq ft it costs ₹87,000; quoted per running ft, the same price is ₹10,875 a foot. A BOQ that asks for "wardrobe, per sq ft" without saying which area gets prices that can't be put side by side.

Write the basis into every modular line, for example: "measured by front elevation area, excluding loft and drawers". The [BOQ checker](/boq/check) flags modular lines that don't, and its dimension box works out the quantity from `8' x 7'6"`.

## Boundary

The rules come from the public copies of IS 1200 Parts 10, 11, 13 and 21 linked below. They are older editions, and newer revisions may differ in detail; check the current edition in the BIS catalogue before relying on a figure in a contract. The modular bases are trade practice, not a standard. Each trade's items, with a line to start from, are in the [item library](/boq/items).

title: Variation orders in interior work, priced from the BOQ
answer: A variation order records a change after the BOQ is agreed: what was added, omitted or substituted, at what rate, and its effect on time and payment, signed before the work is done. CPWD's contract conditions price a changed item at its BOQ rate, a new item at a market rate claimed within 15 days, and extend time in proportion to the added cost.
description: How to record and price changes after an interior BOQ is agreed, using the CPWD contract's clause 12 as the model: rates, new items, time.

body:
## What a variation order is

Once a client accepts a quotation built on a BOQ, every later change is a variation: an extra item, a line dropped, a material swapped, a quantity that grew on site. A [variation order](/systems/variation-order) writes that change down with its price and its effect on time before the work is done, so the final bill is the BOQ plus a short list of approved changes, not an argument.

In interior work most variations are substitutions (veneer instead of laminate, a different tile), additions (a loft nobody drew) and quantities that move once walls are measured.

## The model: CPWD's clause 12

Private interior contracts aren't bound by government rules, but the Central Public Works Department's General Conditions of Contract give a tested structure for changes. Clause 12 says, in short:

- **Changes are made in writing.** The engineer in charge may alter, omit, add or substitute work by a signed written instruction, and the changed work becomes part of the contract.
- **A changed item keeps its contract price.** Altered or substituted work is done on the same conditions, including price, as the main work, unless the rules below apply.
- **A new item gets a market rate, claimed quickly.** For an item not in the contract, the contractor claims a market rate within 15 days, backed by a rate analysis and invoices; the engineer decides the rate within 45 days.
- **Quantities far above the BOQ can be re-rated.** Where a contract item exceeds the limit set in the contract's schedule, the rate for the excess quantity can be revised the same way.
- **Time moves with cost.** The completion time is extended in proportion to the added cost against the original contract value, plus 25% of that extra time.

## What to write on a variation order

1. **Which line it changes**: the BOQ line number and its description, or "new item".
2. **What changes**: added, omitted, substituted or quantity revised, with the new description written as fully as a BOQ line (board and grade, thickness, finish, hardware, unit and measurement basis).
3. **The rate and where it comes from**: the BOQ rate if the item is already in the BOQ; a new rate with its rate analysis if it isn't.
4. **The amount, plus or minus**, and GST on it.
5. **Effect on time**: the extra days, worked out the same way as clause 12 or as agreed.
6. **Effect on payment**: which payment stage it is billed with.
7. **Signatures and date**, before the work starts.

## Pricing a change from the BOQ

Most of the price is already in the BOQ. A wardrobe that grows from 60 to 72 sq ft by front elevation is 12 more sq ft at the agreed rate. A swap from laminate to veneer shutters is the difference between two rates, each built from material, labour and wastage. An omission is a credit at the BOQ rate.

This only works if the BOQ line said what was priced. "Wardrobe, per sq ft" gives nothing to price a change against; a line that names the board, thickness, finish, hardware and [measurement basis](/systems/measurement-basis) does. The [measurement rules](/boq/measurement-rules) and [material specifications](/boq/material-specifications) are where those lines are settled.

## Agree the rules before the first change

Put the variation rules in the quotation's terms: changes only in writing, the BOQ rate for listed items, how a new item is priced, and how much quantity can grow before its rate is reopened. Ahrom Labs' own default terms for a design studio's quotations include "work not listed here, or changed after acceptance, is quoted separately as a variation".

## Boundary

The clause 12 summary is from the CPWD General Conditions of Contract for construction works, April 2026 edition; it binds government works under that contract, not a private interior job. Use it as a model and put your own rules in your contract. The schedule limits it refers to vary by contract and are not given here.

title: What is a BOQ? BOQ vs estimate, quotation and BOM
answer: A bill of quantities (BOQ) lists every item of work with its description, unit and quantity, measured from the drawings before anyone prices it. Contractors fill in the rates, so three quotes can be compared line by line. An estimate is the expected cost, a quotation is a priced offer, and a BOM lists the parts of one product.
description: What a BOQ is in interior work, and how it differs from an estimate, a quotation, a BOM, a rate analysis and a schedule of rates.

image.alt: A ruled bill of quantities on the left and a signed, sealed quotation on the right, with a calculator between them.

sources.title: Delhi Schedule of Rates (DSR)
IS 1200, Method of measurement of building and civil engineering works (all parts)

body:
## What a BOQ is

A [BOQ](/systems/bill-of-quantities) is the list of work, not the price of it ([what one looks like in Excel](/boq/template)). Each line names one item (a wardrobe, a ceiling, a wiring point), says what it is made of, gives the unit it is measured in and the quantity measured from the drawings. The rate and amount columns stay empty until someone prices them.

Its job is to make prices comparable. When three contractors price the same lines, the quotes differ only in rates, and a cheap quote can't hide a thinner board or a missing loft.

## BOQ, estimate, quotation, BOM: the difference

| Document | Who makes it | What it holds | Binding? |
|---|---|---|---|
| BOQ | Designer or quantity surveyor | Items, descriptions, units, quantities | No; it is the basis for prices |
| Estimate | Designer or owner | The BOQ with expected rates: what the job should cost | No; internal |
| Quotation | Contractor or the design-build studio | Rates, amounts, taxes, terms, validity | Yes, once accepted |
| BOM | Manufacturer or workshop | Every part and material to make one product | No; it drives buying and cutting |

The BOM and the BOQ meet in a workshop. The client's BOQ has one line for a wardrobe priced by area; the workshop's BOM for that wardrobe lists the sheets of plywood, the laminate, the edge band and each hinge.

## Rate analysis and schedules of rates

A rate analysis breaks one item's rate into material, labour, wastage, overheads and profit. It is how a contractor arrives at the rate in a BOQ line, and how a designer checks one that looks too low.

A schedule of rates is a published list of item rates. For central government works, the Central Public Works Department publishes the Delhi Schedule of Rates (DSR). It is a reference for how items are described and priced in government work, not a price list for private interiors in another city.

## Lump sums, provisional sums and PC sums

- **Lump sum**: one price for a defined scope ("bathroom CP fittings, LS"). Quick to write, but it hides what's inside; split it into named items wherever you can.
- **Provisional sum**: an allowance for work not yet defined, adjusted when it is.
- **Prime cost (PC) sum**: an allowance for something the client will choose later, such as tiles at a stated rate per sq ft, adjusted to the actual price.

When a provisional or PC sum is settled, or anything else changes after the BOQ is agreed, it is recorded as a [variation order](/boq/variation-orders).

## Boundary

This page explains the documents; it does not give rates. How each interior item is measured and specified is in the [item library](/boq/items), and the [checker](/boq/check) reads a BOQ from Excel and shows what each line leaves open.

title: Indian compliance requirements for an ERP: audit trail, e-invoice, e-way bill, MSME, TDS

body:
## Which rules apply to you

Most rules turn on two facts: whether the business is a company, and its turnover. The [requirements builder](/erp/check) applies these for you.

| Rule | Applies when | What the ERP must do |
|---|---|---|
| Audit trail | A company keeps its books in software | Log every change with its date; can't be switched off |
| E-invoice (IRN) | Aggregate turnover above ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18 | Get an IRN for each B2B invoice, credit and debit note |
| 30-day IRP limit | Annual aggregate turnover ₹10 crore and above | Report each e-invoice within 30 days of its date |
| E-way bill | Goods move with a consignment value above ₹50,000 | Produce the e-way bill from the dispatch |
| MSME payment limit | Buying from a micro or small enterprise | Track each bill's due date, at most 45 days from acceptance |
| TDS on purchase of goods | A buyer with turnover above ₹10 crore in the previous year | Track each seller's yearly total; deduct beyond ₹50 lakh |
| Personal data | Holding digital personal data of staff, customers or contacts | Reasonable security safeguards; breaches can be traced (rules on how: from May 2027) |

## Audit trail: every company keeping books in software

Since 1 April 2023, a company that keeps its books in accounting software must use software that records an [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail) of every transaction: an edit log of each change, with its date, that cannot be disabled. The rule is a proviso to rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, inserted in March 2021 and deferred twice to 1 April 2023. The company's auditor reports on it.

For an ERP that keeps the books, this means the old value, the new value, who changed it and when, for every entry, with no setting anywhere that turns it off. It also means no gap at cutover: the trail has to run through the move from the old system to the new one. See the [audit-trail requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail).

## E-invoice, and the 30-day limit

From 1 August 2023, registered persons whose aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 must [e-invoice](/systems/e-invoice): each B2B invoice, credit note and debit note is registered on the invoice registration portal (IRP), which returns an IRN and a signed QR code. Notification 10/2023–Central Tax lowered the threshold from ₹10 crore.

From 1 April 2025, taxpayers with annual aggregate turnover of ₹10 crore and above cannot report a document to the IRP more than 30 days after its date; the portal refuses it. An ERP for such a business should show which invoices are still unreported and how many days each has left. See the [e-invoice requirements](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice).

## E-way bill

Under rule 138 of the CGST Rules, an [e-way bill](/systems/e-way-bill) is needed before goods move with a consignment value exceeding ₹50,000. The ERP should produce it from the invoice and the dispatch, not have someone retype the consignment into the portal at the gate. See the [e-way bill requirement](/erp/requirements#dispatch-eway-bill).

## MSME payment limits, and why they matter for tax

Section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006 (the [MSME payment rule](/systems/msme-payment-rule)) requires a buyer to pay a micro or small enterprise supplier by the agreed date, and the agreed period can never exceed 45 days from acceptance; with no written agreement, the Act's appointed day applies. Section 16 adds compound interest on late payment.

The Income-tax Act, 2025, in section 37(2)(g), allows the deduction for an amount owed to such a supplier only when it is actually paid, if it is paid beyond that limit, and the usual grace until the return due date doesn't apply to it. So the ERP needs to know which suppliers are micro or small enterprises, and show each of their bills with its due date. How the rule applies to a particular business, a trader for example, is a question for your CA. See the [MSME requirements](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates).

## TDS on purchase of goods

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, a buyer whose turnover exceeded ₹10 crore in the preceding tax year deducts tax on payments to a seller for goods beyond ₹50 lakh in the year ([TDS on purchases](/systems/tds-on-purchases)) (section 393(1), table row 8(ii), formerly section 194Q). The provision is a table, so it is cited here rather than quoted: read row 8(ii) and its note in the Act. The ERP has to keep each seller's running total for the year and start deducting on the bill that crosses it. See the [TDS requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-tds-purchases).

## Personal data

A business holding digital personal data, of employees, customers or contacts, is a data fiduciary under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Section 8 requires reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach and intimation of a breach in the prescribed way. For an ERP, that means access to personal details limited by role and logged, and a way to see who saw what. The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (13 November 2025) set out how: the safeguards (rule 6) and breach intimation, including a detailed report to the Board within 72 hours (rule 7), come into force eighteen months after publication, in May 2027 (rule 1(4)). The Act's own sections are brought into force by separate notification, so check which are in force when you buy. If the system comes with an AI assistant, see [what it sends out](/ai-assistant/data-safety). See the [personal-data requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-personal-data).

## What changed, and when

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| 7 Mar 2018 | Rule 138 substituted: e-way bill above ₹50,000 |
| 24 Mar 2021 | Audit-trail proviso added to the Companies (Accounts) Rules |
| 31 Mar 2022 | Audit trail deferred to financial years from 1 April 2023 |
| 1 Aug 2023 | E-invoice threshold lowered to ₹5 crore |
| 11 Aug 2023 | Digital Personal Data Protection Act published |
| 1 Apr 2025 | 30-day IRP reporting limit extended to ₹10 crore and above |
| 1 Apr 2026 | Income-tax Act, 2025 in force: MSME rule in section 37(2)(g), TDS on goods in section 393 |

## What to ask a vendor

Ask the vendor to do each test on the checklist, in front of you: change an entry and show the audit trail; generate an IRN for a test invoice; list the invoices that are near the 30-day limit; produce an e-way bill from a dispatch; show an MSME supplier's bills with due dates. A vendor who can't show it doesn't have it yet. Ahrom Labs states its own gaps the same way: it has not yet built an IRP connection, and its e-way bill client is built but not yet live.

title: ERP contract checklist: code ownership, licence, AMC and your data
answer: Before a custom ERP is built, settle in writing who owns the code, what the licence covers and for how long, what the annual maintenance contract includes and costs, how changes are priced, how fast support answers, and how your data comes out at any time. Both ownership models are fair if they are stated.
description: ERP contract checklist for India: code ownership, licence term, AMC scope and cost, change pricing, support time, data export and DPDP terms.

body:
## Two ownership models, both fair if stated

Custom software in India is sold in one of two ways, and buyers often don't find out which until they try to leave.

| | You own the code | The vendor licenses it |
|---|---|---|
| What you pay for | The build, and the code is handed over | A working system and a licence to use it |
| After the build | You can take it to any developer | The licence runs with the maintenance contract |
| Usually costs | More up front, plus whoever maintains it | Less up front, plus the annual contract |
| Risk to watch | Code nobody else can maintain without documentation | Losing the licence if the contract ends |

Neither is wrong. What is wrong is not knowing which one you signed.

## Clauses to settle before the build

1. **Ownership.** Who owns the source code and the software. If it's licensed, what the licence covers and for how long. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-ownership))
2. **Your data.** That you can export all your business data, in standard formats, at any time, including at the end. Data you can't take out ties you tighter than any clause. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-data-export))
3. **Pricing.** Fixed price per phase, quoted before each phase starts, or time and materials, with a cap. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-fixed-phases))
4. **Changes.** How a change is written down, priced and agreed before it is built. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-changes))
5. **The maintenance contract.** What it covers (licence, hosting, fixes, small changes), what it costs per year, and what is quoted separately. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#contract-amc-scope))
6. **Support.** Response time in writing, and documentation that lets another developer take the system over. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-support))
7. **Hosting and storage.** Who pays for the server and the storage, and whether storage costs are passed on at the provider's price.
8. **Personal data.** If the vendor processes personal data on your behalf (staff, customers, contacts), the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 requires a valid contract for that: section 8(2). Name the vendor's duties for safeguards and breach intimation in it.

## How Ahrom Labs does it

Stated plainly, as on the [engagement page](/engagement):

- **Ahrom Labs owns the code.** You get a working system and a licence to use it for as long as the annual maintenance contract runs; the source code stays with Ahrom Labs. If the contract stops, the licence ends with it.
- **Your data is yours** and can be exported at any time.
- **Fixed price per phase**, after a short fixed-fee modeling phase; a change is priced and agreed before it is built.
- **The AMC is 15–21% of the project value per year**, covering the licence, the server, fixes and small changes; a new module is its own phase.
- **Support** requests are answered within 48 hours at most, and every system ships with a system document any developer or agent can pick it up from.

If you need to own the code outright, say so before the build; it changes the price and the hand-over, and it is better settled first than discovered later.

title: ERP implementation plan: phases from mapping the business to go-live
answer: A custom ERP goes live in phases, each in use before the next starts: a short modeling phase that maps the business and ends with a dated, fixed-price plan; then the records that must be right; then the daily work of each department; then reports and AI. Data migration is its own scoped piece of work, and the requirements' tests are the acceptance tests for each phase.
description: ERP implementation plan for Indian manufacturers and traders: phases from modeling to go-live, migration, acceptance tests, timeline and cost.

image.alt: A path of five stepping stones leading to a flag.

body:
## Why phases, each in use before the next

ERP projects in Indian SMEs usually fail the same way: people go back to Excel and WhatsApp because the system doesn't match how the business runs, and the old data turns out messier than anyone planned for. Phases that each go live and get used before the next one starts catch both early. You never pay for months of work you can't see, and a wrong assumption costs a phase, not the project.

## The phases

| Phase | What it delivers | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Modeling | A map of the business (entities, workflows, approvals, rules) and a dated plan with a fixed price per phase | The owner agrees the map and the plan |
| 1. Records that must be right | Masters, stock, opening balances, the ledger or the Tally link; migration of what's needed | Counts and balances tie to the old system |
| 2. Daily work, department by department | Sales, purchase, stores, production, dispatch, accounts, as the plan orders them | Each department works in the system, not beside it |
| 3. Portals | Customer and supplier access | Customers and suppliers use their links |
| 4. Reports and AI | Dashboards from the same records; assistants and document reading with human review | Figures trace to records; AI answers match the reports |

The order inside phase 2 comes from the map: whatever the business can least afford to get wrong goes first.

## Data migration is its own piece of work

Migration is scoped and quoted separately, before it starts, rather than discovered halfway. Every import is checked against its source, doubtful rows are held for a person, and each import is tagged so it can be removed as one batch. See [moving from Tally](/erp/tally-migration).

## The requirements are the acceptance tests

Every line on the [requirements checklist](/erp/requirements) has a test. Before a phase is signed off, run the tests for the lines it covers, on your own data. The same tests made the [vendor demo script](/erp/vendor-demo-script); using them again at go-live is how you find out whether what was shown is what was built.

## How long it takes

It depends on how new the problem is. Something already built for another business can ship in days or weeks; genuinely new ground takes a couple of months, delivered in phases so part of it is in use early. The modeling phase ends with a date for each phase, so you know the timeline before you commit to the build.

## What it costs

Published 2026 guides from other firms put a custom ERP for a small Indian manufacturer at roughly ₹3–15 lakh, and a fuller build for a mid-sized manufacturer at ₹15–40 lakh. Those are market figures, not a price list: two businesses that both want "an ERP" can need very different systems, which is why the price is fixed per phase only after the modeling phase. Maintenance after go-live usually runs as an annual contract. Ahrom Labs' terms, and the sources for those ranges, are on the [engagement page](/engagement); what to settle in the contract is in the [contract checklist](/erp/contract-checklist).

## Your plan, in one line per phase

Write the plan as a table: phase, what it delivers, the requirement lines it covers, the acceptance tests, the date, the price. If a vendor can't fill that table before the build, the plan isn't ready.

title: ERP for interior design firms and fit-out businesses: what to require
answer: An interior design or fit-out business needs quotations built from a BOQ, projects that show what each is waiting on, vendor and freight charges checked against agreed rates, labour logged against each job and payroll computed from attendance, and, where there are sister companies, each invoicing on its own letterhead and GSTIN from one system.
description: ERP requirements for interior design and fit-out firms in India: BOQ quotations, project blockers, vendor rate checks, payroll, two companies.

image.alt: A drafting table with a floor plan pinned to it and a roll of drawings.

body:
## Start with these

1. **Quotations from a BOQ**, with revisions kept and the accepted one turned into the order without retyping. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#sales-quotation-format)) How to write the BOQ itself is in the [interior BOQ guide](/boq).
2. **What each project is waiting on**: material, drawing, approval or payment, worked out fresh each time. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-blockers))
3. **Vendor and freight charges checked** against agreed rates, with overcharges flagged. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#purchase-rate-check))
4. **Labour logged against each job**, so job costs include it. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#payroll-work-logs))
5. **Payroll computed** from attendance, rates and advances, never typed. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#payroll-computed))
6. **Two companies, one system**: each invoice under its own company's letterhead and GSTIN, from one client list. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#sales-multi-company))
7. **Staff see only their own cash entries**, and bank data is refused to them by the system. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-role-access))

## The rules that usually apply

- **Being a company:** the books need an [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail). ([audit trail](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail))
- **Above ₹5 crore:** e-invoices for B2B work. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- **Paying micro and small vendors:** due dates at most 45 days from acceptance. ([MSME](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates))

All of them, quoted from the official text: [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).

## What this looks like in a running system

Savistar, an interior design studio, and Saag, its sister furniture workshop, run one system: projects and site visits for Savistar, workshop orders for Saag, and one combined finance ledger. Each invoice picks its own company's letterhead, logo and GSTIN; vendor and freight charges are checked against reference rates; payroll is days × rate − advances, never typed; and an AI assistant answers from their own records in English or Hinglish. Quotations are built from a BOQ library, with payment stages that become invoices. See [software for interior design firms](/industries/interior-design-and-furniture), or try the [interiors demo](https://interiors-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), where one freight trip is overcharged on purpose.

## Build your list

The [requirements builder](/erp/check) with "Project businesses" selected gives the full list for your turnover and whether Tally stays.

If the system will have an AI assistant, [what it should answer for this kind of business](/ai-assistant/interior-design-firms) lists the questions, with what Atelier AI answers today.

title: Is your business ready for an ERP? A 10-question self-check
answer: A business is ready for an ERP when someone owns each process, the masters are clean enough to load, the owner will decide disputes between departments, and people will record work where it happens. Ten questions, each with what to fix first if the answer is no.
description: ERP readiness checklist for Indian manufacturers and traders: ten questions on processes, masters, owners and data, and what to fix first.

image.alt: A hand placing the top block on a small pyramid of building blocks.

body:
## The ten questions

Answer each yes or no. Each no is something to fix before, or as the first phase of, any system.

1. **Can you draw how an order moves**, from enquiry to payment, with who does what at each step? If not, that map is the first piece of work; a system built on the wrong picture makes the workarounds faster.
2. **Does each process have one owner** who can say how it should work? Without one, the system inherits every disagreement.
3. **Are your masters clean?** One record per customer, supplier and item, with GSTINs and HSN codes that are right. Duplicates in Tally become duplicates in the ERP.
4. **Do you know your stock** to the level you pick and ship (a reel, a box, a plate), or only as totals? If only totals, plan a stock count before go-live.
5. **Is there one place for each number?** If the same figure lives in Tally, a spreadsheet and someone's notebook, decide now which one is the truth.
6. **Will people record work where it happens**, on a phone on the floor or at site, rather than at a desk at day end?
7. **Will the owner decide** when sales and production disagree about how something should work? Systems fail more often from undecided questions than from code.
8. **Do you know which compliance rules apply?** Turnover decides [e-invoicing](/systems/e-invoice) and its 30-day limit; being a company decides the [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail). See [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).
9. **Have you decided about Tally?** Keep it as the books, or move the books into the new system. See [moving from Tally](/erp/tally-migration).
10. **Can you name the first thing the system must get right?** The records that must be right come first; everything else is a later phase.

## Scoring it

- **8 to 10 yes:** ready. Write your requirements with the [builder](/erp/check) and start talking to vendors.
- **5 to 7:** ready if the first phase is mapping the business and cleaning masters, not building screens.
- **Under 5:** start with the map. Buying a system before the processes are decided is how ERP projects stall.

## Why this order

Ahrom Labs starts every engagement with a short modeling phase that answers most of these questions: what exists, who owns it, which records must be right, and what each phase delivers. You keep the model and the plan whether or not you continue. See [how an engagement runs](/engagement) and the [requirements checklist](/erp/requirements).

title: ERP selection matrix for India: Tally, ERPNext, Odoo, SAP Business One or custom
answer: TallyPrime, ERPNext, Odoo and SAP Business One all handle Indian e-invoicing in some form; they differ in how they're licensed, where they run, and how far they bend to your process. A custom system fits the process exactly but has to be built. Score them against your own requirements, weighted by your priorities, not against a vendor's feature list.
description: ERP selection criteria for India: TallyPrime, ERPNext, Odoo, SAP Business One and custom, compared on licence, hosting, e-invoice and fit.

image.alt: A balance scale with one box on each pan, level.

Generate e-Invoice (IRN) and print QR code in TallyPrime

India fiscal localization (e-invoicing and e-way bill), Odoo 20.0
