SAP Business One

body:
## How to use this matrix

Don't pick a system from a feature table, this one included. Every option below can be made to look good in a demo. Pick from your own requirements:

1. Build your list with the [requirements builder](/erp/check) and set a priority on each line.
2. Send the same [Excel template](/erp/template) to each option, one copy per vendor. It scores Yes, Partly and No against your priorities.
3. Make each vendor do the [demo tests](/erp/vendor-demo-script) for your Must lines. A yes you didn't see counts as partly.

The table below is for the first cut: which options to invite at all. Each fact is from the product's own documentation, linked under sources.

## The matrix

| | TallyPrime | ERPNext | Odoo | SAP Business One | Custom-built |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | Accounting and inventory software from Tally Solutions | Open-source ERP from Frappe | ERP suite of apps, Community and Enterprise editions | SAP's ERP for small businesses | A system built around your process |
| Licence | Proprietary licence | GPL-3.0 (open source) | Community: LGPLv3; Enterprise: Odoo's own licence | Proprietary licence | As your contract says: you own the code, or a licence runs with maintenance |
| Where it runs | Your PC or server; TallyPrime's integration gateway listens only on that machine | Self-hosted or Frappe Cloud | Odoo Online, Odoo.sh or on-premise | Cloud or on-premise | Wherever it's built for |
| E-invoice and e-way bill | Built in: IRN, QR code and e-way bill from the sales voucher | Through the India Compliance app (GST, e-invoice, e-way bill, TDS) | India localization modules for e-invoicing (from 15.0) and e-way bill | Through India localization and partner add-ons; check with your partner | Built to the NIC specs, or not at all; ask |
| Audit trail (edit log) | Edit log; a separate release keeps it always on | Check it meets the rule | Check it meets the rule | Check it meets the rule | Must be built in and can't be switched off |
| Fit to your process | You adapt to it | Configurable; customised by developers | Configurable; customised by developers or partners | Configured by partners | The process is modeled first, then built |
| Works alongside Tally | Is Tally | Replaces it, or runs beside it with an integration | Replaces it, or runs beside it with an integration | Replaces it, or runs beside it with an integration | Either: posts into Tally, or keeps the books itself |

"Check it meets the rule" means the product's documentation we read doesn't say, in plain terms, that the edit log meets the [audit-trail rule](/erp/compliance): a log of every change with its date that can't be disabled. Ask the vendor to show it.

## When each one tends to fit

- **TallyPrime alone**: accounting-led businesses whose operations fit in its inventory, and who mainly need GST done right. When it stops being enough is in [seven signs you've outgrown Tally](/notes/outgrown-tally-signs).
- **ERPNext or Odoo**: businesses whose processes are close to the standard modules, with a partner or in-house developer to configure and maintain them.
- **SAP Business One**: small businesses that want an established vendor and a partner-led implementation.
- **Custom**: when the process is the business's edge, the standard modules force workarounds, or the system has to do something no package does (an IBR statutory folder from certificates, reel-level reservations, two companies on one ledger).

The longer comparison for manufacturers is [Tally, ERPNext, Odoo or a custom ERP](/notes/tally-vs-erpnext-vs-custom-erp).

## What the matrix leaves out

Price, deliberately: licence, implementation and maintenance costs change by edition, users and partner, and a number here would be wrong for most readers. Get quotes against the same requirements list, and settle ownership and data export before signing: see the [contract checklist](/erp/contract-checklist). Ahrom Labs builds custom systems, so read this page as a builder's view; the facts about each product are from its own documentation.

title: ERP for small manufacturers in India: the requirements that matter most
answer: A small Indian manufacturer needs an ERP that works from its existing Excel BOMs, tracks material down to the plate or batch it cuts from, sets stock aside for each order, costs jobs from what was actually used, and keeps the GST books or posts cleanly into Tally. Above ₹5 crore turnover add e-invoicing; as a company, an audit trail.
description: ERP requirements for small manufacturers in India: BOM import, traceability, remnants, job costing, reservations, GST or Tally, e-invoice.

image.alt: A small hydraulic workshop press with its hand pump.

body:
## Start with these

The lines a small manufacturer can least afford to get wrong, in the order they usually go live. Each links to its test.

1. **Your BOMs, from Excel.** Import the sheets you already keep, matched to the item master; a likely typo suggested, never silently corrected. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-bom-import))
2. **A released BOM is frozen.** Purchase and stores work from a version, not a moving sheet. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-bom-release))
3. **Shortfalls become purchase requests**, after stock and usable remnants are counted. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#purchase-need-to-request))
4. **Remnants go back into stock**, with weights from dimensions, offered to waiting BOM lines before anything is bought. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-cutting-remnants))
5. **Jobs costed from actual use**, material and labour. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-costing-from-use))
6. **What each job is waiting on**, worked out fresh, not typed. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#production-blockers))
7. **Certificates kept once and linked to what they cover**, with any link that ends in statutory paperwork confirmed by a person. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#quality-confirmed-links))

## The rules your turnover brings in

- **Being a company:** the books need an [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail) that can't be switched off. ([audit trail](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail))
- **Above ₹5 crore:** e-invoices for B2B sales; **at ₹10 crore and above:** reported within 30 days. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- **Buying from micro and small enterprises:** due dates at most 45 days from acceptance. ([MSME](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates))

All of them, quoted from the official text, are in [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).

## What this looks like in a running system

At a boiler and pressure-vessel manufacturer, Ahrom Labs' system imported six of the client's real BOM files through the interface, traces each plate and section through cutting, and assembled each boiler's [IBR statutory folder](/systems/ibr-statutory-folder) from a bank of [material test certificates](/systems/material-test-certificate). In a live cut test, a 157.00 kg plate became 127.17 kg used, 15.70 kg remnant and 14.13 kg scrap, conserved exactly. The same system keeps the books: GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, TDS and 23 reports, with Tally optional. See [ERP for boiler and pressure-vessel manufacturers](/industries/boiler-pressure-vessel-manufacturing), or try it with twelve sample logins, one per department, at the [manufacturing demo](https://boiler-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo).

## Build your list

The [requirements builder](/erp/check) with "Manufacturing" selected gives the full list for your turnover and whether Tally stays, ready to send to vendors.

If the system will have an AI assistant, [what it should answer for this kind of business](/ai-assistant/manufacturers) lists the questions, with what Ember AI answers today.

title: Moving from Tally to an ERP: what to migrate and how to check it
answer: Decide first whether Tally stays as the books or goes. Then move masters, opening balances, outstanding bills, stock with its batches, and the history people actually look up, each checked against its source: count the rows, hold anything that matches two records for a person, and tag every import so it can be removed as a batch. Keep the audit trail unbroken through the switch.
description: How to move from Tally to an ERP in India: keep Tally or replace it, what to migrate, how to check each import, and the audit-trail rule at cutover.

image.alt: Two filing cabinets with an open box of files between them.

sources.title: Companies (Accounts) Second Amendment Rules, 2022 (G.S.R. 235(E))
sources.publisher: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Gazette of India

checks.quote: the figures, letters and words “1st day of April, 2023” shall be substituted

body:
## Keep Tally, or replace it?

Both work, and the choice decides what you migrate.

- **Tally stays as the books.** The ERP runs sales, stock and operations, and posts approved invoices into TallyPrime as vouchers. Your accountant keeps working in Tally. Very little accounting history moves; what moves is masters and open items. LS Technologies runs this way: approved invoices reach TallyPrime within 30 seconds, and every posted voucher is checked against Tally's own data.
- **The ERP keeps the books.** Ledgers, GST returns and TDS move into the ERP, and Tally becomes optional or goes. More moves, and the [audit trail](/systems/audit-trail) has to carry across. A boiler manufacturer Ahrom Labs built for runs this way, with GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and TDS from the operations system.

How each connection to Tally works, and why TallyPrime needs an agent on its own PC, is in [four ways to connect a business system to TallyPrime](/notes/connecting-tallyprime-four-ways).

## What to move

| What | Why it matters | How to check it |
|---|---|---|
| Ledger and party masters | Every transaction hangs off them | Count before and after; no duplicates by GSTIN |
| Item masters, with units and HSN | Stock and tax depend on them | Count; every HSN valid; units consistent |
| Opening balances | The books must agree on day one | Trial balance in the ERP equals Tally's on the cutover date |
| Outstanding bills (receivable and payable) | Collections and payments continue | Each party's total matches Tally's outstanding |
| Stock, with batches or units | Reservations and costing need it | Quantity and value per item match; batches or units as labelled |
| GST history you look up | Returns and notices refer back | The periods you need, read-only, with their filing status |
| Sales history (enquiries, quotations, orders) | Sales can't work without it | Row counts; doubtful rows held, not guessed |

## How to check each import

Three rules, from moving five years of a manufacturer's sales history (see [the note](/notes/sales-history-moved-without-guessing)):

1. **Check the file against itself first.** A broken export had shifted 154 of 20,167 diary rows by a column or two; read naively, they would have lost their status. All 20,167 were recovered by checking each row's known last columns.
2. **Hold, don't guess.** A quotation that matched no customer, or more than one, went to a review list: 2,221 matched exactly one customer and came in; 303 waited for a person.
3. **Tag every import.** Each row carries the import it came from, so a batch found wrong later can be removed as one.

## Cutover and the audit trail

A company keeping its books in software must have an audit trail for every financial year from 1 April 2023 (the date was substituted by the Companies (Accounts) Second Amendment Rules, 2022). Plan the cutover so the trail doesn't break: close a period in Tally, move balances as at that date, and start the ERP's trail from the first entry after. Keep Tally's data for the years before, read-only, for the auditor. See the [audit-trail requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail-date).

## A sequence that works

1. Freeze masters for a week; clean duplicates in Tally first.
2. Move masters, then check counts.
3. Pick a cutover date at a period end.
4. Move opening balances and outstanding bills as at that date; tie the trial balance.
5. Move stock and check quantity and value per item.
6. Run both systems for one cycle if Tally stays as the books; compare.
7. Move history last, read-only, and hold doubtful rows for a person.

See also the [migration requirement](/erp/requirements#sales-history-migration) and the [Tally integration requirements](/erp/requirements#integrations-tally).

title: ERP for trading and distribution businesses in India: what to require
answer: A trading or distribution business needs stock tracked by the unit it picks and ships, reserved against each customer order so nothing is sold twice, moved by scanning across stores, purchase documents read in without retyping, and invoices that reach Tally or the GST books automatically. Above ₹5 crore, e-invoices; at ₹10 crore and above, the 30-day limit and TDS on large purchases.
description: ERP requirements for trading and distribution in India: unit-level stock, reservations, scanning, AI-read bills, Tally posting, e-invoice, TDS.

image.alt: Cartons stacked on a pallet, with a handheld barcode scanner beside them.

body:
## Start with these

1. **Stock by the unit you ship**: a reel, a box, a carton, each with its own label, not only a total. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-unit-level))
2. **Reserved against each order line**, so a reserved unit can't go to another customer without a manager's override. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-reservations))
3. **Moved by scanning**, in, out and between stores, including a partner's. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-scan-moves))
4. **Staff entries approved** before they change stock. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#stores-approval))
5. **Purchase documents read by AI and checked by a person**: invoices, freight bills, bills of entry, bank statements. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#reporting-extraction-review))
6. **Every supplier bill matched** to its order and what was received. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#purchase-three-way-match))
7. **Invoices into Tally automatically**, each checked against Tally's own data, if Tally stays as the books. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#accounts-tally-posting))
8. **Customers follow their own orders** on a portal that never shows stock or other customers. ([requirement](/erp/requirements#portals-no-stock-exposure))

## The rules your turnover brings in

- **Above ₹5 crore:** e-invoices; **at ₹10 crore and above:** reported within 30 days. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- **As a buyer with turnover above ₹10 crore:** [TDS on purchases](/systems/tds-on-purchases) from a seller beyond ₹50 lakh in the year. ([TDS on purchases](/erp/requirements#accounts-tds-purchases))
- **Goods moving above ₹50,000:** [e-way bills](/systems/e-way-bill). ([e-way bill](/erp/requirements#dispatch-eway-bill))

All of them, quoted from the official text: [compliance requirements](/erp/compliance).

## What this looks like in a running system

At LS Technologies, an electronics-component importer and trader, each reel carries its own QR label; 5,256 live reels moved to a two-store model with none lost. Reels are reserved per customer PO line, oldest first. Five document types, bills of entry included, are read by AI at 88–95% zero-correction, each approved by a person, and approved invoices post into TallyPrime as vouchers within 30 seconds. See [software for electronics-component traders](/industries/electronics-component-trading), or scan reels yourself in the [trading demo](https://electronics-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo).

## Build your list

The [requirements builder](/erp/check) with "Trading and distribution" selected gives the full list for your turnover and whether Tally stays.

If the system will have an AI assistant, [what it should answer for this kind of business](/ai-assistant/trading-distribution) lists the questions, with what Ohm AI answers today.

title: ERP vendor demo script: what to make every vendor show you
answer: Don't let an ERP vendor run their own demo. Bring your own data, give them a list of tests, and watch them do each one: change an entry and show the audit trail, reserve stock and try to ship it elsewhere, post an invoice to Tally and delete it there. A yes you didn't see demonstrated is a partly.
description: ERP vendor demo script for Indian manufacturers and traders: the tests to make every vendor do in front of you, by department, and red flags.

image.alt: A laptop on a stand showing a dashboard, with a stopwatch beside it.

body:
## How to run the demo

A vendor's own demo shows what their product does well, on data made to look good. Yours should show whether it does what your business needs, on data that looks like yours.

1. **Send the tests a week ahead.** The vendor should know what they'll be asked; a vendor who can't prepare for a known test won't handle an unknown one.
2. **Bring your own data.** A real BOM, a real supplier bill, ten real stock items. Sample data hides the edge cases you live with.
3. **You drive, or you call every click.** Watching a smooth run-through tells you little; asking "now change that" tells you a lot.
4. **Score as you go.** Yes only for what you saw done. Use the [Excel template](/erp/template): it has a column for each answer and scores vendors for you.
5. **Keep the script.** The same tests are your acceptance tests before go-live.

## The tests, by department

Pick the ones that apply from the [requirements builder](/erp/check). These are the ones most often promised and least often shown.

**Accounts**
- Enter a purchase bill, change its amount, and show the edit log with the old value, the new value, the user and the time. Then show there is no setting that turns the log off. ([audit trail](/erp/requirements#accounts-audit-trail))
- If your turnover is above ₹5 crore: generate an IRN for a test invoice and show the QR code on the print. ([e-invoice](/erp/requirements#accounts-e-invoice))
- Lock last month and try to edit an invoice in it. ([period lock](/erp/requirements#accounts-period-lock))
- If Tally stays: approve an invoice, find the voucher in TallyPrime, delete it there, and show it flagged after the next sync. ([Tally posting](/erp/requirements#accounts-tally-posting))

**Stores**
- Receive two units of the same item with different quantities and show each with its own label. ([unit-level stock](/erp/requirements#stores-unit-level))
- Reserve a unit for one order, then try to ship it on another. ([reservations](/erp/requirements#stores-reservations))
- Show the movements behind one item's balance, and that they add up to it exactly. ([derived balances](/erp/requirements#stores-balances-derived))

**Purchase**
- Receive less than ordered, enter the bill for the full quantity, and show the mismatch flagged before approval. ([three-way match](/erp/requirements#purchase-three-way-match))
- Mark a supplier as a micro enterprise and show its bills with due dates. ([MSME](/erp/requirements#purchase-msme-due-dates))

**Production**
- Import one of your real BOM sheets and show how each unmatched line is handled. ([BOM import](/erp/requirements#production-bom-import))
- Cut a plate and show the remnant back in stock with its weight. ([remnants](/erp/requirements#production-cutting-remnants))

**Access and reliability**
- Sign in as staff and open a bank page directly by its address. It should refuse. ([role access](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-role-access))
- Pull the network cable during a sync and show what happens to the queued entries. ([offline](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-offline))
- Ask for a full export of the demo data and open it in Excel. ([data export](/erp/requirements#nonfunctional-data-export))

**AI**
- Ask the assistant this month's sales, then compare its answer with the sales report. A number that doesn't match is the answer to whether you can trust it. ([assistant](/erp/requirements#reporting-assistant-no-invented-numbers); the full set of tests for an AI assistant is in the [AI assistant vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test))

## What a demo won't tell you

Some answers only come in writing:

- **Who owns the code**, and what you hold if you stop paying. See the [contract checklist](/erp/contract-checklist).
- **How changes are priced** after the contract is signed.
- **Support response time**, and who else could take the system over.
- **A reference customer** like you, whom you call yourself.

## Red flags

- "That's on the roadmap" for a Must line.
- A demo only on the vendor's own sample company.
- "It's configurable" without configuring it in front of you.
- An AI feature that can't show where its numbers came from.
- No written answer on code ownership or data export.

## Try the tests on a live system

Every test above can be tried today on Ahrom Labs' demos, with sample data that resets nightly: [manufacturing](https://boiler-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), [trading](https://electronics-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo) and [interiors](https://interiors-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo). Use them to see what a pass looks like before you watch anyone else's demo.

title: AI in ERP: what it can safely do today
answer: AI in an ERP is safe and useful today in three jobs: answering questions from your own records through fixed, read-only look-ups; reading documents such as invoices and purchase orders into drafts a person checks; and drafting suggestions a person approves. It isn't safe yet letting a model post entries, set prices or commit dates by itself, because a model can be confidently wrong. Judge any "AI ERP" by what it may change without a person, and how it proves its numbers.
description: AI in ERP explained for owners: the three safe uses today, what not to let it do alone, AI-native claims, and how to test any ERP's AI before buying.

image.alt: A brass desk lamp lighting an open steel card-index drawer, one card raised: finding the one right record.

body:
## Three jobs AI does well in an ERP

| Job | What it looks like | What keeps it safe |
|---|---|---|
| **Answering questions** | "Who owes us money?", "Which orders are late?" in plain words | The model only picks the question; code runs a [fixed look-up](/systems/fixed-look-up) and a [grounding check](/systems/grounding-check) drops any sentence with a number not in the result ([how it works](/ai-assistant/how-it-works)) |
| **Reading documents** | Supplier invoices, purchase orders, freight bills and bank statements turned into draft entries | Every draft goes through a person before it is posted |
| **Drafting suggestions** | A likely match, a reorder list, a draft reply, a task | The suggestion is read-only until someone accepts it |

These are not hypothetical. Our assistants Atelier AI, Ohm AI and Ember AI answer from live business records this way ([the question library](/ai-assistant/questions) lists every question and whether it's live), and in LS Technologies' system, an electronic components trader's, 88–95% of extracted documents need no correction depending on the type, and every one is still reviewed before it is posted ([AI extraction with a person in the loop](/notes/ai-extraction-human-in-the-loop)).

## What not to let it do alone

- **Post accounting entries.** An entry that's 99% right is a wrong ledger. Extraction drafts; a person approves.
- **Set prices or quote.** Pricing rules belong in code you can read; AI can draft the inputs, such as quantities read from a drawing.
- **Commit dates or schedule machines.** A schedule has hard limits (machine hours, routing order, material on hand) that a rule or solver can guarantee and a language model can't ([where AI fits in scheduling](/manufacturing/production-scheduling-software)).
- **Decide on documents that carry your name to a customer or inspector.** Even a very accurate suggestion should wait for a person there. We run two matchers with the same scoring, one that auto-applies and one that never does, for exactly that reason ([same confidence, different autonomy](/notes/same-confidence-different-autonomy)).

The rule of thumb: AI drafts and explains; code and people decide anything that changes a record.

## "AI-native ERP" and other claims

Vendors now describe ERPs as AI-native, AI-first or agentic. The label tells you little. Three questions tell you a lot:

1. **What can the AI change without a person?** Listing, drafting and answering are low risk. Posting, ordering and emailing customers are not.
2. **Where do its numbers come from?** A model writing its own database queries, or summarising rows, will occasionally produce a figure that's nearly right ([AI hallucination](/systems/ai-hallucination)). A fixed look-up gives the same figure as the report every time.
3. **What happens when it doesn't know?** A good assistant says "the data doesn't have that". A weak one answers anyway.

## How to test it before you buy

Bring your own questions and your own documents to the demo:

- Ask five questions you already know the answers to from your reports, and compare every number. The [number check](/ai-assistant/number-check) flags any figure in an answer that isn't in the source data.
- Ask it to mark an invoice paid or delete an order. Nothing should change without a person pressing save.
- Give it a supplier invoice it hasn't seen and look at what it gets wrong, not what it gets right.
- Ask something the system can't know, like next month's demand from a customer who hasn't ordered.

The full list, with what passing and failing looks like, is in [how to test an AI assistant before you buy it](/ai-assistant/vendor-test). For choosing the ERP underneath, see [ERP for job shops](/manufacturing/job-shop-erp).

title: AI assistant for construction contractors: what it answers
answer: A contractor's assistant should answer whether each site is making money, which sites haven't sent today's report, what material is in the godown and at each site, which running bills are waiting and who owes money, all from the contractor's own records and matching its screens. Datum AI does this in a construction contractor's system, which anyone can try on the public demo, and refuses site staff the money, margin and payroll questions.
description: An AI assistant for construction contractors: the site, material, billing and labour questions it should answer from your own records, and how to check it.
body:
A contractor's work is spread over sites: daily reports from each one, material in the godown and on site, machines moving between them, labour, site cash, and running bills that wait weeks to be certified. The director's questions cut across all of it: is this site making money, who hasn't reported today, who owes us and how late. An assistant earns its place if it answers those in one line, with the same figures as the screens.

## What should it answer?

Every question Datum AI answers is listed below, with the screen to check each answer against. They cover one site end to end, margin against the estimate, daily reports filed and missing, material used against the BOQ norm, stock by location, idle machines, site cash, running-account bills and receivables by age, the cash book and the bank, attendance, KYC and gate passes, the wage register, and the trading desk's orders and supplier rates.

## What should it refuse?

Advice, changes to records, and anything a login can't see on the screens. A site engineer asking whether a site is making money should get a refusal, not a margin; "mark the bill paid" should get a pointer to the Billing tab, not a changed bill.

## How Datum AI does it

Datum AI is the assistant in a construction contractor's system: a waterproofing and repair contractor that also trades construction chemicals. A small model picks one of its [fixed look-ups](/systems/fixed-look-up); code runs it with the same maths as the screens, so a site's margin is the Dashboard's margin and an RA bill's amount is the Billing tab's. Site engineers and storekeepers get the site questions but not company money, margins or payroll. "Remind me to call them on Friday" drafts a task that is saved only when the person presses Save. [How it works](/ai-assistant/how-it-works) sets out the design.

You can ask it two questions yourself on the [construction demo](https://construction-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), from any sample login, with sample sites, workers and bills.

## How to check a vendor's

Run the [vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test) on a copy of your own sites, and paste its written answers into the [number check](/ai-assistant/number-check) with the dashboard beside them. Ask about one site's margin, then work it out by hand from its approved work, material, labour and site cash: the two should match.

title: What an AI assistant sends out, and the data laws that apply
answer: Ask what is sent to the AI provider with each question. It is one of three things: the question only, the question with the rows of the answer, or your records themselves. Ahrom Labs' assistants send the question only by default. In India the DPDP Act keeps the business responsible for safeguards, breach notice and erasure, including at its AI provider, from May 2027; in the US, state privacy laws and the FTC set the rules.

body:
An AI assistant on your system sends something to an AI provider every time someone asks a question. Whether that is safe depends on exactly what is sent, so start there, and get the vendor's answer in writing.

## What is sent with each question?

There are three designs, and they send very different amounts:

| Design | What goes to the AI provider | Ahrom Labs' assistants |
|---|---|---|
| The model only chooses | The question, and the one before it for follow-ups | Atelier AI and Ohm AI by default; Ember AI for how-to answers (the question and the help-guide sections picked) |
| The model writes the answer | The question and the rows of the answer | Atelier AI when a person picks a voice for it; Ohm AI in its "write" answer mode; Ember AI's live-data answers, built and switched off at the client |
| The model reads your records | Documents or tables, loaded so it can "understand the business" | None |

In the first design the ledger never leaves: the model picks a look-up and a period, and your own system runs it and builds the table. [How it works](/ai-assistant/how-it-works) explains the design. The second design sends a few rows per answer: not the database, but your data, so you should be able to switch it off. The third sends the most: ask what, how often, and where it is kept.

Ember AI's live-data answers are switched on only when the client's approver is recorded by name in Settings, because in that mode the rows of each answer go to the writing model. On the public demo they are on, with a sample company.

## Can the assistant change anything?

It shouldn't be able to. Look-ups should be read-only queries, so the worst a wrong choice can do is show the wrong table. "Remind me to call them on Friday" should draft a task that a person saves. Ask it to mark an invoice paid or delete an order, and check nothing changed: test 6 of the [vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test#read-only).

## Can a junior staff member ask what they can't see?

Only if the assistant ignores the screens' rules. Each look-up should run as the signed-in person, with the same limits as the screens:

- **Atelier AI:** staff see only their own tasks and cash entries; payroll, advances and bank statements are refused to them.
- **Ohm AI:** answers LS Technologies' own staff, never the partner store's logins or customers; its settings are for the admin.
- **Ember AI:** answers each person from the guides of their own departments, and each live-data look-up follows the same department limits as the screens.

Test it with a junior login.

## Whose account does it run on, and what does it cost?

The business's own. Ahrom Labs' assistants use the client's own key with the AI provider (OpenRouter), set in the system's Settings, so the client pays the provider directly and can switch it off at any time. A daily question limit caps the cost: at LS Technologies it is about a hundredth of a rupee per question. Ask a vendor whose key it is, what the limit is, and what happens when the credit runs out.

## What happens when the AI provider is down?

The screens carry on as before, and the assistant should get simpler, not wrong. In Savistar's system a keyword router takes over, so answers get less clever but the figures still come from the same look-ups.

## What does India's DPDP Act ask of the business?

If the assistant handles personal data (names and details of staff, customers or contacts), the business is the Data Fiduciary and the AI provider is its Data Processor. The duties stay with the business:

| Duty | Where it is | Starts |
|---|---|---|
| Reasonable security safeguards, including at the processor | Act section 8(5); rule 6 | May 2027 |
| A valid contract with the processor, with safeguards in it | Act section 8(2); rule 6(1)(f) | May 2027 |
| Breach notice to the Data Protection Board and each person affected, without delay, then a detailed report to the Board within 72 hours | Act section 8(6); rule 7 | May 2027 |
| Erase the data when consent is withdrawn or the purpose is served, and cause the processor to erase it | Act section 8(7) | With the rule on retention, rule 8: May 2027 |
| Transfer outside India allowed, subject to requirements the Government may set | Act section 16; rule 15 | May 2027 |

"May 2027" is rule 1(4): the rules that set out these duties come into force eighteen months after the Rules were published on 13 November 2025. Rules on the Data Protection Board itself are already in force. The Act's own sections are brought into force by separate notification, so check which are in force on the date you sign.

What it means for an assistant, in practice:

- **Know where the model runs.** A provider like OpenRouter routes to models run outside India. That is allowed under rule 15, but you should know which countries, and that the contract covers it.
- **Send only what the answer needs.** The question-only design sends no personal data unless the question itself contains some.
- **Put it in the contract.** Safeguards, breach notice to you, and erasure at the provider, as rule 6(1)(f) and section 8(7) expect.

How the Act applies to your business is a question for your lawyer. The same rules, for the system underneath, are in the [ERP compliance guide](/erp/compliance).

## What applies in the US?

The US has no single federal law for the personal data a business keeps. Instead:

- **State privacy laws.** A growing number of states have their own, California's CCPA the best known. They mostly reach larger businesses and those that buy or sell personal data, and they give people rights to know, delete and opt out.
- **The FTC.** The Federal Trade Commission can act against a business whose data practices are unfair or deceptive, including security that falls short of what it promised.
- **Your contracts.** Customers and insurers often ask for security terms of their own.

The practice is the same as in India: know where the model runs, send only what the answer needs, and put safeguards, breach notice and deletion at the provider in the contract. Which laws reach your business is a question for your lawyer.

title: How an AI assistant answers without inventing numbers
answer: The design that keeps figures right has four parts: a small AI model only chooses which question is being asked; code runs a fixed, read-only look-up with the same maths as the app's screens; any written sentence with a number that isn't in the result is dropped; and questions the data can't answer get a plain "the data doesn't have that". The model never produces a figure.
description: How the design works, for buyers: the model picks the question, code runs a fixed look-up, and sentences with numbers not in the data are dropped.

image.alt: A wooden pigeonhole rack with one card in a single slot.

body:
Most AI assistants on business data let the model produce the answer's figures, either by writing a database query ([text-to-SQL](/systems/text-to-sql)) or by reading rows and summarising them. Both work most of the time, and that is the problem: an owner can't tell the answer that is right from the one that is nearly right (an [AI hallucination](/systems/ai-hallucination)). The design below takes the figures away from the model altogether. It is how [Atelier AI, Ohm AI and Ember AI](/ai-assistant/questions) work.

## Step 1: the model only chooses

A small AI model reads the question and picks from fixed options: what kind of question it is (a figure, how to do something, a reminder, small talk, something the data can't answer), which look-up fits, which period, and whether it follows on from the last question. It returns a choice, not text. Names in the question (a client, an item, a reel number) are matched to real records by code; when two records could match, Ohm AI, for one, asks which one is meant.

## Step 2: code runs a fixed look-up

Each question type has a [fixed look-up](/systems/fixed-look-up): a read-only query written in advance, with only the values filled in. It uses the same maths as the app's own screens, so "who owes us money?" counts the same invoices, the same way, as the unpaid-invoices screen. The answer is shown as a table, with a link to that screen.

Because the look-ups only read, the assistant can't change anything. "Remind me to call them on Friday" drafts a task that is saved only when the person presses Save.

## Step 3: words are checked against the table

A sentence above the table is optional, in the voice the person picked. Before it is shown, a [grounding check](/systems/grounding-check) compares every number in it with the table. If any number isn't there, such as a total the writer added up, a percentage it worked out or a figure it rounded, the sentence is dropped and only the table is shown. You can run the same check on any assistant with the [number check](/ai-assistant/number-check).

## Step 4: it says what it can't answer

Advice ("should we raise prices?") and data the system doesn't hold get a plain "the data doesn't have that", with questions it can answer instead. Every question it couldn't answer, and every thumbs-down, is listed for the owner, so the next look-up to add comes from what people actually asked.

## How is it tested?

Each assistant has its own set of real questions, run through the real pipeline before it goes live: plain English, fragments, typos and Hinglish. Atelier AI routed 55 of 55 test questions and 57 unseen real phrasings correctly. The questions each assistant answers are in the [question library](/ai-assistant/questions).

## What does it cost to run?

Very little, because the model only makes a choice. At LS Technologies it is about a hundredth of a rupee per question, on the client's own AI account, with a daily question limit. What is sent to the AI provider is set out in [what leaves your server](/ai-assistant/data-safety).

## What it doesn't do

It doesn't answer questions nobody built a look-up for, and it doesn't search documents. Questions over drawings, certificates and past decisions are a different design, [retrieval and knowledge graphs](/services/rag-knowledge-graphs), where each answer shows the document it came from. The full engineering note is [an assistant that only answers from your own records](/notes/assistant-that-answers-from-your-ledger).

title: AI assistant for interior design firms: what it answers
answer: An interior design firm's assistant should answer how each project is going, who owes money, which workshop orders are late, what material is still to come and whether a project made money, all from the firm's own records and matching its screens. Atelier AI does this at Savistar & Saag today, in English and Hinglish, and refuses staff the payroll and bank questions.
description: An AI assistant for interior designers and furniture workshops: the questions it should answer from your own projects, invoices and orders, and how to check it.

image.alt: A fan of fabric and wood-veneer swatches beside a rolled tape measure.

body:
A design studio runs on projects, quotations, site visits, a workshop and a lot of money owed. The owner's questions cut across all of them: how is this client's project going, who still owes us, are we delivering on time. An assistant earns its place if it answers those in one line, with the same figures as the screens.

## What should it answer?

Every question Atelier AI answers today is listed below, with the screen to check each answer against. Atelier AI runs at an Indian studio, so its money questions say GST; a US studio asks the same ones with sales tax. They cut across the whole firm: one project end to end, money owed and billed with the GST split, quotations waiting and won, late workshop orders and on-time delivery, material still to come, attendance and payroll, the cash book and the bank, and whether a project made money.

## What should it refuse?

Advice ("should we raise our design fee?") and anything a login can't see on the screens. A site supervisor asking for payroll should get a refusal, not a figure.

## How Atelier AI does it

[Atelier AI](/notes/assistant-that-answers-from-your-ledger) is the assistant in Savistar & Saag, an interior design studio and a furniture workshop sharing one system. A small model picks one of its [fixed look-ups](/systems/fixed-look-up); code runs it with the same maths as the screens. It routed 55 of 55 test questions and 57 unseen real phrasings correctly, including Hinglish. Each person can pick a voice for it, and a written line with a number not in the table is dropped. "Remind me to call them on Friday" drafts a task that is saved only when the person presses Save.

You can ask it two questions yourself on the [interiors demo](https://interiors-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), from any sample login.

## How to check a vendor's

Run the [vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test) on a copy of your own projects, and paste its written answers into the [number check](/ai-assistant/number-check) with the finance screen beside them. If the assistant comes with a new system, the [ERP guide for interior design firms](/erp/interior-design-firms) lists what the system itself should do.

title: AI assistant for manufacturers: where to start
answer: For a manufacturer, start with how-to questions answered from the system's own help guide, for each person's departments, and add live-data questions (stock, purchase orders, approvals) once the owner has decided what may be sent to the AI provider. That is where Ember AI stands at a boiler manufacturer: how-to answers live, live data built and switched off.
description: An AI assistant for a manufacturing ERP: start with how-to answers from your own help guide, then stock, purchase and approval questions, and how to check it.

image.alt: A round steel pressure gauge on a short pipe stub.

body:
A manufacturing system has many departments and many screens, and most questions on the shop floor and in the office are "how do I". That is the safest place for an assistant to start: the answers come from the system's own help guide, and no business data leaves.

## Step 1: how-to answers from your own guide

The assistant picks the right section of the help guide for the question, from the departments the person works in, and answers from it with a link to the screen. Questions like:

- How do I raise a purchase request?
- How do I send a packing list for approval before dispatch?
- How do I assign test certificates to units?
- Where do I change my password?

Unrelated questions ("write me a poem") should get a fixed reply that never reaches a writing model. Each person gets a daily question limit set per department.

## Step 2: live data, when the owner decides

Stock on hand, items below minimum, purchase orders not received, an order's value and payments, approvals waiting. These need a decision first: in a design where the rows are worded by a writing model, the rows of each answer are sent to the AI provider. The owner should approve that by name, and each look-up should follow the same department limits as the screens. The [data safety guide](/ai-assistant/data-safety) sets out what to ask.

## How Ember AI does it

Ember AI is the assistant in a boiler manufacturer's system, open to staff. How-to answers are live; the live-data look-ups are built and switched off until the client records its approval. Job-card and work-in-progress questions are not built yet. On the [boiler demo](https://boiler-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo), with a sample company, live data is on: anyone can ask it two questions. Every question it handles is listed below.

## How to check a vendor's

Ask ten how-to questions from your own process and follow the answers: do the steps work? Then run the [vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test). For the system itself, see the [ERP guide for small manufacturers](/erp/small-manufacturers).

title: AI assistant for traders and distributors: what it answers
answer: A trader's assistant should answer stock by item and store, what is running low or not moving, what came in and went out, where a particular reel or box is, which purchase orders are waiting, and which customers have stopped ordering. Ohm AI does this for LS Technologies' own staff today, and says "the data doesn't have that" when asked about money the system doesn't hold.
description: An AI assistant for traders and distributors: the stock, shipment and customer questions it should answer from your own records, and how to check it.

image.alt: A reel of electronic components on carrier tape, partly unspooled.

body:
A trading business asks the same few questions all day: do we have it, where is it, what went out, who hasn't ordered. The answers are in the stock records already; an assistant saves opening four reports to get them.

## What should it answer?

Every question Ohm AI answers today is listed below, each with the report to check the answer against. The core of it: stock by item and store, what is running low or not moving, what came in and went out, where a particular reel or box is, purchase orders and approvals, and two plain-arithmetic statistics: which items will run out at the recent shipping rate, and which customers have gone quiet against their own usual gap between orders. Each statistic says how much history it used, and "and last month?" keeps the customer and the item.

## What should it refuse?

Questions about data the system doesn't keep. A stock system that doesn't hold receivables should say so when asked what a customer owes, not produce a figure.

## How Ohm AI does it

Ohm AI is the assistant in LS Technologies' inventory system, for its own staff; the partner store's logins and customers don't get it. A small model picks one of its fixed read-only look-ups; code resolves item, customer and reel names and runs the query. Questions it couldn't answer, and every thumbs-down, are listed in Settings, so the next look-up comes from what was asked. It runs on LS Technologies' own key with a daily question limit, at about a hundredth of a rupee per question. On the [electronics demo](https://electronics-erp.ahromlabs.com/demo) anyone can ask it two questions about a sample company.

## How to check a vendor's

Pick five items you know the stock of, and ask in the demo. Then run the [vendor test](/ai-assistant/vendor-test) and compare its written answers with the stock summary in the [number check](/ai-assistant/number-check). For the system underneath, see the [ERP guide for trading and distribution](/erp/trading-distribution).

title: ASME vs IBR 2026: how the two boiler codes fit together
question: Does IBR accept ASME boilers and materials?
answer: In India a boiler is registered under the Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026, whatever code it was designed to. IBR 2026 does accept ASME in defined ways: ASME materials, ASME welding consumables and NDT certificates, ASME-designed parts where IBR has no provision, and inspection of export boilers to a foreign code with a Form I Part A certificate.
description: ASME BPVC vs IBR 2026 side by side: who approves, inspects and stamps, the forms, and every place IBR 2026 accepts ASME, quoted from the Gazette.

sources.publisher: Central Boilers Board, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade

sources.title: Boiler and Pressure Vessel Certificates of Authorization and the Certification Mark: Informational Handbook (BPV-GUI-03)

the inspecting authority may inspect any boiler meant for export during the various stages of its construction to comply with the requirements of any foreign code and may grant a certificate in Part-A of Form-I.

design and construction of boiler or boiler component is in accordance with international code or standard including British Standards (BS), European Standards (EN), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code

checks.quote: In addition to the above, materials conforming to IS or to any of the International codes BS, EN, ASME, DIN and JIS can also be used.
Specifications for Filler Alloys (SFA) of American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Part IIC
Level-III NDT Certificates from Indian Society for Non-destructive Testing(I.S.N.T.) or American Society for Non-destructive Testing( A.S.N.T.)
The tubes of boilers and heat exchangers made of titanium and other exotic metals may be approved as per international codes, including American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME)

body:
## Side by side

| | ASME BPVC | IBR 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | A private standard, given legal force by US states and Canadian provinces that adopt it | Statutory regulations under the Boilers Act, 2025, in force across India |
| Written by | ASME committees | The Central Boilers Board |
| Covers | Boilers, pressure vessels, nuclear, transport tanks | Boilers, steam pipes and their parts (pressure vessels are outside IBR) |
| Shop approval | ASME certificate, after a joint review ([U and S stamps](/asme/u-stamp)) | Recognition as a manufacturer by class, under IBR 2026 |
| Independent inspection | [Authorized Inspector](/asme/authorized-inspector) from an accredited agency | Inspecting Authority, Competent Person |
| Record of the item | [Manufacturer's Data Report](/asme/data-reports) (P-2, P-3, U-1) | Forms: Inspecting Authority's certificate (Form I), maker's certificate (Form IV), material certificates (Form V) |
| Welders | Section IX qualification ([WPQ](/asme/wps-pqr-wpq)) | IBR welder certificate |
| In service | NBIC and the jurisdiction | IBR registration, periodic inspection and certificate for use |

The biggest practical difference: in India IBR applies to **boilers and steam pipes**, while unfired pressure vessels are not regulated by IBR at all (vessels for compressed gases fall under PESO's Static and Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules instead); in the US, a pressure vessel is usually regulated by the state and built to [Section VIII](/asme/section-viii).

## Where IBR 2026 accepts ASME

Quoted from the Gazette below:

- **Parts IBR doesn't cover** may be designed, made, inspected and certified to the ASME Code (among others), with the Inspecting Authority's permission (regulation 3(4)).
- **Exotic tubes** (titanium and the like) may be approved to ASME and other international codes (regulation 3(5)).
- **Export boilers** may be inspected by an Indian Inspecting Authority to a foreign code and certified in Form I Part A (regulation 4). See [buying from India](/asme/buying-from-india) and [IBR Form I Part A](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-a).
- **Exemption** of a boiler or component built to an international code, ASME included, on conditions (regulation 5).
- **Materials** to ASME (and IS, BS, EN, DIN, JIS) may be used; IBR's own material table lists ASME SA and SB specifications by name (regulation 30); the [materials list](/asme/items) shows which common ones it names. See [Section II](/asme/section-ii).
- **Electrodes** are classified to ASME Section II Part C (SFA) or AWS specifications (regulation 71).
- **NDT personnel** with ASNT certificates are accepted alongside ISNT (regulation 7). See [Section V](/asme/section-v).

## What a shop working to both needs

An Indian boiler maker building to ASME for export and to IBR at home keeps two sets of approvals, two sets of welder qualifications and two report formats over the same welds and materials. The records underneath are the same: [heat numbers](/asme/mtr), welders, procedures, NDE, tests. That's the case for keeping them once and printing either set of forms; the IBR side is covered in the [IBR 2026 guide](/ibr) and [boiler registration documents](/ibr/registration-documents).

title: Authorized Inspector and AIA: who inspects ASME work
question: What does an ASME Authorized Inspector do?
answer: An Authorized Inspector is the independent third party on every stamped ASME boiler or vessel. They work for an Authorized Inspection Agency (usually an insurance company or a state), hold a National Board commission, check the design, materials, welding and NDE, witness the pressure test and sign the data report. No signature, no stamp.
description: The ASME Authorized Inspector (AI) and Inspection Agency (AIA): who they are, the National Board commission, what they check and sign.

sources.title: Boiler and Pressure Vessel Certificates of Authorization and the Certification Mark: Informational Handbook (BPV-GUI-03)
Accreditation programs for repairs, alterations and relief valve testing (R, VR, NR, T/O)
sources.publisher: The National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors

checks.quote: for most of the ASME Certificates of Authorization to use the ASME Certification Mark, an agreement with an ASME Accredited Authorized Inspection Agency (AIA) is required.

body:
## The people and the organizations

- **Authorized Inspection Agency (AIA)**: an organization accredited by ASME to provide inspection for Code construction. Most are insurance companies that write boiler and machinery cover; some are state or provincial jurisdictions acting as their own agency.
- **Authorized Inspector (AI)**: the agency's employee who does the inspecting. They hold a National Board commission with the endorsement for new construction, earned through education, experience and an examination.
- **AI Supervisor**: the agency's senior inspector who oversees the AI and takes part in joint reviews and audits.

A shop can't hire an AI on its own; it signs an inspection agreement with an agency, which assigns the inspector. Most ASME certificates require that agreement before ASME will schedule a [joint review](/asme/u-stamp).

## What the Inspector does on a job

- Reviews the design calculations and drawings for Code compliance.
- Checks material against its [MTR](/asme/mtr) and its marking.
- Checks that every weld is made to a qualified [WPS](/asme/wps-pqr-wpq) by a qualified welder, and that welders are in [continuity](/asme/welder-continuity).
- Reviews NDE results and heat treatment records.
- Witnesses the [hydrostatic or pneumatic test](/asme/hydrostatic-test).
- Signs the [data report](/asme/data-reports) and authorizes the stamping.

The shop's quality control manual names the Inspector's hold points: the steps where work stops until the AI has seen it.

## The Inspector is not the shop's QC

The AI checks that the shop's system worked; they don't run it. If the shop's own inspection is missing, the AI reports it as a nonconformity rather than doing it for them.

## Repairs in service

Repairs and alterations to equipment already installed are inspected by a National Board commissioned inspector under the NBIC, with the repair company holding the National Board R stamp. See [National Board registration and the R stamp](/asme/national-board-registration).

title: ASME B31.1 vs B31.3: power piping and process piping
question: What is the difference between ASME B31.1 and B31.3?
answer: B31.1 is the Power Piping code, for steam and water systems in power plants and boiler external piping. B31.3 is the Process Piping code, for refineries, chemical, pharmaceutical and similar plants, with fluid service categories that scale the rules to the hazard. Neither is part of the Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, but both use Section IX for welding.
description: ASME B31.1 power piping vs B31.3 process piping: scope, boiler external piping, fluid service categories, examination, hydrotest pressure and welding.

sources.title: B31.1 Power Piping

body:
## Side by side

| | B31.1 Power Piping | B31.3 Process Piping |
|---|---|---|
| Typical plants | Power stations, central heating and cooling plants, industrial steam systems | Refineries, chemical, petrochemical, pharmaceutical, food, gas processing |
| Special scope | Boiler external piping (BEP) | Fluid service categories: Normal, Category D, Category M, High Pressure, High Purity |
| Hazard approach | One set of rules, conservative | Rules scale with the fluid's hazard |
| Hydrostatic test | 1.5 × design pressure | 1.5 × design pressure, adjusted by the stress ratio at temperature |
| Welding qualification | Section IX | Section IX (with B31.3's own additions) |
| Stamp | BEP by a Section I certificate holder; otherwise none | None |

## Boiler external piping

The piping from a power boiler out to the first stop valve and beyond, as Section I defines it, is **boiler external piping**. It is designed to B31.1 but is part of the Section I boiler: built by a holder of a Section I certificate (S, A or PP) and inspected by the [Authorized Inspector](/asme/authorized-inspector). See [Section I vs Section IV](/asme/section-i-vs-iv).

## B31.3 fluid service categories

- **Normal**: most services.
- **Category D**: non-flammable, non-toxic fluids at low pressure and moderate temperature; lighter rules.
- **Category M**: fluids where a single small exposure can cause serious harm; stricter rules.
- **High Pressure** and **High Purity**: chapters of their own.

The owner is responsible for assigning the category.

## What carries over from the BPVC

- Welding procedures and welders are qualified to [Section IX](/asme/section-ix); a shop's [WPS and PQR](/asme/wps-pqr-wpq) can serve both its vessel and piping work where the variables fit.
- NDE methods come from [Section V](/asme/section-v); the piping code sets how much and the acceptance criteria.
- Materials are mostly ASME or ASTM specifications; see [Section II](/asme/section-ii).

Piping test pressures follow the same logic as vessels: see the [hydrostatic test](/asme/hydrostatic-test) guide.

title: ASME BPVC sections I to XIII explained
question: What are the sections of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code?
answer: The ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code has thirteen sections. Construction sections set the rules for a product: I for power boilers, IV for heating boilers, VIII for pressure vessels, X and XII for plastic vessels and transport tanks, III for nuclear. Reference sections serve them all: II for materials, V for testing, IX for welding, XIII for relief devices.
description: The 13 sections of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code: what each covers, which ones a boiler or pressure vessel shop needs, and how they fit together.

sources.title: 2025 ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code
Boiler and Pressure Vessel Certificates of Authorization and the Certification Mark: Informational Handbook (BPV-GUI-03)

checks.quote: Subscription to the indicated sections of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code is required for certification to assure that Code users have the latest applicable Code rules.

body:
## Construction sections and reference sections

The Code is easiest to read as two kinds of book. A **construction section** is the rulebook for one kind of equipment: what it may be made of, how it is designed, welded, examined, tested and stamped. A **reference section** holds rules that several construction sections point to, so they aren't written out again in each.

A pressure vessel shop working to Section VIII Division 1 therefore also works to Section II (materials), Section V (nondestructive examination), Section IX (welding) and Section XIII (relief devices), because Division 1 sends it there.

## The thirteen sections

| Section | Title, in short | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| I | Power boilers | Construction |
| II | Materials (Parts A to D) | Reference |
| III | Nuclear facility components | Construction |
| IV | Heating boilers | Construction |
| V | Nondestructive examination | Reference |
| VI | Care and operation of heating boilers | Recommended practice |
| VII | Care of power boilers | Recommended practice |
| VIII | Pressure vessels (Divisions 1, 2 and 3) | Construction |
| IX | Welding, brazing and fusing qualifications | Reference |
| X | Fiber-reinforced plastic pressure vessels | Construction |
| XI | Inservice inspection of nuclear plants | Inspection |
| XII | Transport tanks | Construction |
| XIII | Overpressure protection | Reference |

Sections VI and VII are recommendations for owners, not construction rules, and nothing is stamped to them. Section XI applies to nuclear plants in service.

## Which sections a shop needs

- **Pressure vessels**: [Section VIII](/asme/section-viii) (usually Division 1), plus II Part A or B for the material, II Part C if it buys filler metal to an SFA specification, II Part D for allowable stresses, V, [IX](/asme/section-ix) and XIII.
- **Power boilers** (steam above 15 psi (1 bar), hot water above 160 psi (11 bar) or 250 °F (121 °C)): Section I with the same reference sections. Below those limits, a heating boiler is built to Section IV; see [Section I vs Section IV](/asme/section-i-vs-iv).
- **Relief valves and rupture disks**: [Section XIII](/asme/section-xiii).

To hold an ASME certificate, a shop must own current copies of the sections its scope uses (ASME lists them per certificate as its "required code books"); photocopies are not accepted at the joint review.

## How the sections are numbered inside

Each construction section uses letter prefixes for its parts, which is why paragraph numbers look the way they do. In Section VIII Division 1, UG paragraphs are general requirements for every vessel, UW is welded construction, UCS is carbon and low-alloy steel and UHA is high-alloy steel. Section I uses PG for general requirements and PW for welding; Section IX uses QW for welding. A reference such as UG-27 therefore reads "Section VIII Division 1, general requirements, paragraph 27": the [shell thickness rules](/asme/shell-thickness).

## Editions

The whole Code is republished every two years; the current one is the 2025 Edition. How editions, code cases and interpretations work is in [ASME Code editions](/asme/editions).

title: Buying ASME-stamped vessels and boilers from India
question: Can an Indian manufacturer build an ASME U-stamped pressure vessel?
answer: Yes. An Indian fabricator holding an ASME U certificate builds and stamps Section VIII vessels to the same rules and with the same Authorized Inspector involvement as a US shop. For a US installation, also check National Board registration and the state's rules. For boilers, IBR 2026 lets an Indian Inspecting Authority certify an export boiler to a foreign code.

body:
## Why buyers look at India

India has a large base of fabricators building boilers, pressure vessels and heat exchangers for refineries, power and process plants, many with ASME certificates for export work, and engineering and fabrication rates below US levels. The Code is the same wherever the shop is: a U stamp from a shop in Gujarat means what one from Texas does.

## What to check before ordering

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| The certificate covers the work | Designator (U, U2, S, PP), scope (shop or field), and that it is current; ask for a copy and confirm on ASME's certificate holder listing. See [ASME stamps](/asme/stamps) |
| Who the Authorized Inspection Agency is | The AIA named on their agreement; the [Authorized Inspector](/asme/authorized-inspector) signs your [data report](/asme/data-reports) |
| National Board registration | If your state requires NB registration (most do), the shop must be authorized to register. See [National Board registration](/asme/national-board-registration) |
| The edition | Name the Code edition in the order; see [editions](/asme/editions) |
| Your jurisdiction's own rules | Some states and every Canadian province add requirements; see [US and Canadian boiler laws](/asme/state-boiler-laws) |
| Materials | SA specifications with MTRs, and where the mill is. See [MTRs](/asme/mtr) |
| Documents | The full package in English: calculations, drawings, MTRs, WPS/PQR, welder records, NDE, PWHT charts, test record, data report |

## Boilers: the IBR side

For a boiler, the Indian Boiler Regulations add a step at home. Regulation 4 of IBR 2026 lets an Indian Inspecting Authority inspect a boiler meant for export, through its stages of construction, against a foreign code such as ASME, and certify it in Form I Part A. That certificate is for India's records; it doesn't replace the ASME stamp or the Authorized Inspector. See [ASME vs IBR 2026](/asme/asme-vs-ibr) and [IBR Form I Part A](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-a).

## Managing the order

- **Inspection and test plan**: agree hold points (material review, fit-up, NDE, PWHT, hydrostatic test) and who witnesses each, yours and the AI's.
- **Document review before shipping**: get the data report package as a draft before the vessel ships, not with it.
- **Logistics**: oversized vessels need shipping planned early; the data report and nameplate must match what arrives.

## Records that travel well

A buyer overseas sees a shop through its documents. Shops that keep heat numbers, welders and NDE in one system send a complete package on the day the vessel is ready; that is the system we build.

title: ASME data reports: U-1, U-1A, U-2, P-2 and H-2 forms
question: What is an ASME U-1A form?
answer: A Manufacturer's Data Report is the record of what a stamped boiler or pressure vessel is: its design conditions, materials, thicknesses, joints, examinations and test pressure, signed by the manufacturer and the Authorized Inspector. U-1 and U-1A are for Section VIII Division 1 vessels, U-2 for parts, P-2 and P-3 for Section I boilers, H-2 for heating boilers.
description: ASME Manufacturer's Data Reports: which form for which item (U-1, U-1A, U-2, A-1, P-2, P-3, H-2), what goes in them, who signs, and National Board registration.

sources.title: ASME Data Report Forms
Registration
sources.publisher: The National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors

body:
## Which form

ASME publishes the forms free on its website as fillable PDFs. The ones most shops use:

| Item | Form |
|---|---|
| Section VIII Div. 1 vessel | U-1, or U-1A (alternative form for single-chamber vessels) |
| Part of a Div. 1 vessel built by another shop | U-2 or U-2A (partial data report) |
| Plate heat exchanger | U-1P |
| Supplementary sheet, shell-and-tube heat exchanger | U-5 |
| Section VIII Div. 2 vessel | A-1 (A-2 for parts) |
| Section VIII Div. 3 vessel | K-1 |
| Section I boiler, except watertube and electric | P-2 (P-2A electric) |
| Section I watertube boilers, superheaters, waterwalls, economizers | P-3 |
| Section I fabricated piping | P-4A |
| Section IV boiler, except watertube and cast | H-2 (H-3 watertube) |
| Section XIII relief valve or rupture disk | UV-1, HV-1, UD-1 or TV-1 (certificates of conformance) |

The 2025 forms became mandatory with the 2025 Code on 1 January 2026; see [ASME Code editions](/asme/editions).

## What goes in a U-1A

The report describes the vessel as built, not as quoted:

- manufacturer, purchaser and installation location, serial numbers;
- design pressure, [MAWP](/asme/mawp) and coincident temperature, and the [MDMT](/asme/impact-testing);
- for each shell and head: material specification and grade, nominal and corrosion thickness, inside diameter, length, [joint efficiency](/asme/joint-efficiency) and type, radiography;
- nozzles and openings, with their reinforcement;
- heat treatment ([PWHT](/asme/pwht)) and impact testing;
- the [hydrostatic or pneumatic test pressure](/asme/hydrostatic-test);
- code cases used, and parts from other shops (with their U-2 reports attached);
- certification by the manufacturer and by the [Authorized Inspector](/asme/authorized-inspector).

## The data report package

Behind the one-page report sits the file the Inspector checked: calculations, drawings, [MTRs](/asme/mtr), weld map, [WPS, PQR and welder qualifications](/asme/wps-pqr-wpq), NDE reports, heat treatment charts and the test record. Assembling that file at the end of a job is where most shops lose days; building it as the job runs is what the software we write does.

## Registration and keeping it

Section VIII Division 1 requires the manufacturer to keep a copy of the data report for a period set by the Code, or to register it with the National Board, which keeps it permanently. Many US jurisdictions require National Board registration for the item to be installed; the National Board asks for reports within 30 days of certification. See [National Board registration](/asme/national-board-registration).

## In India

The IBR equivalents are the maker's certificate (Form IV Part A) and the Inspecting Authority's certificate (Form I); see [IBR Form I Part A](/ibr/forms/form-i-part-a), [boiler registration documents](/ibr/registration-documents) and [ASME vs IBR 2026](/asme/asme-vs-ibr).

title: ASME 2025 Edition: dates, code cases and interpretations
question: When does the ASME 2025 Edition become mandatory?
answer: ASME publishes the whole Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code every two years and each edition becomes mandatory six months after publication. The 2025 Edition was published on 1 July 2025 and applied from 1 January 2026; the next is due in 2027. Code cases add approved alternatives between editions, and interpretations answer questions on the wording.
description: How ASME Code editions work: the two-year cycle, the 2025 Edition dates, which edition applies to a vessel, code cases, interpretations and data report forms.
